triage.notes: ウガンダ・南スーダンとの国境地帯での人口移動・鉱山活動による拡大懸念が記載されているが、これらの国自体での感染事例は明記されていないため verified_locations には含めない。

article.articleHeadline: Người đàn ông 45 tuổi nguy kịch vì mắc sởi lại tưởng cảm cúm
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: A 45-year-old man in critical condition after contracting measles again, thinking it was the flu.
article.articleSummary: Measles infection in a 45-year-old man at 108 Military Central Hospital in Vietnam progressed to severe complications, prompting hospital treatment on 23 July 2026. The patient, who initially self-treated for what he believed was influenza, presented with fatigue, red eyes, sore throat, diarrhea, and a widespread rash; measles was diagnosed on day five of illness after clinical evaluation and laboratory tests. He developed pneumonia, acute purulent rhinosinusitis, enteritis, and liver injury. Intensive supportive care—including fluid and electrolyte management, fever reduction, treatment of secondary infections, and liver support—led to marked improvement after more than a week. Measles, caused by the measles virus, spreads primarily via respiratory droplets and can remain contagious from four days before to four days after rash onset. Vaccination remains the best prevention; timely care is crucial to prevent severe outcomes, especially in adults with underlying conditions.

article.articleHeadline: कांगो में हिंसा के बीच इबोला से जंग पर संकट, संयुक्त राष्ट्र ने जताई चिंता | Insecurity continues to impact Ebola outbreak response in DR Congo: UN
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Crisis in the fight against Ebola amid violence in Congo; UN expresses concern.
article.articleSummary: Violence in North Kivu, Democratic Republic of Congo, is hampering Ebola response as UN agencies warn. Attacks in the Beni area from July 13–19 killed at least 30 and wounded more than 12, forcing displacement and disrupting humanitarian access to affected communities. With security deteriorating, at least six humanitarian organizations have halted movements in several areas where Ebola is being addressed. By July 20, DR Congo's national health authorities reported 2,473 confirmed Ebola cases across Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uele, and Tshopo provinces. The UN and partners are continuing surveillance, laboratory testing, treatment, and community engagement in affected zones. The outbreak was declared on May 15 and has spread to five provinces; transmission is fueled by population movement, insecurity, artisanal mining, and cross-border movement with Uganda and South Sudan. The UN reiterates calls for civilian protection and safe, uninterrupted humanitarian access.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴでの暴力の中、エボラとの闘いに危機 ― 国連が懸念表明
triage.triage_reason: DRCでエボラ確認2,473例、5州に拡大し、治安悪化により人道支援・対応活動が阻害されている重大な公衆衛生事案であり、国際的拡大リスクも存在するためフルRRAへ進めるべき。
triage.notes: ウガンダ・南スーダンとの越境移動が感染拡大要因として言及されているが、これらは対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsから除外。治安悪化により人道支援団体の活動が停止し、対応能力に深刻な影響が出ている点が特に懸念される。

article.articleHeadline: Can mosquito bites affect your brain? Neurologist explains how Japanese Encephalitis can silently attack the brain during monsoon
article.articleSummary: Japanese Encephalitis (JE) causes brain inflammation and is a major public health risk in Asia, including India. Globally, JE yields about 68,000 clinical cases annually with more than 3 billion people at risk in South-East Asia and the Western Pacific. In 2025 India reported 975 confirmed cases and 110 deaths, with roughly 70% of cases in the north and east; cases surge during and after the monsoon when mosquito breeding peaks. JE spreads via Culex mosquitoes that breed in rice fields, ponds and stagnant water, with the virus cycling among mosquitoes, pigs and water birds; humans are dead-end hosts. Early symptoms resemble other viral illnesses, but brain involvement causes persistent high fever, confusion, seizures, stiff neck, weakness or loss of consciousness, demanding urgent hospital care. Diagnosis combines clinical evaluation, laboratory tests of blood or CSF, and MRI (preferred to CT). There is no antiviral treatment; care is supportive. Among survivors, 30–50% have lasting neurological effects.

triage.headline_ja: 蚊に刺されると脳に影響が出る？神経内科医が解説する、日本脳炎がモンスーン期に静かに脳を襲う仕組み
triage.triage_reason: 本記事は日本脳炎に関する一般的な医学解説・啓発記事であり、モンスーン期の季節性流行についての既知情報の紹介に留まる。新規の異常発生や急増を報じるものではない。
triage.notes: 記事は日本脳炎の病態・症状・診断・2025年のインドにおける統計（975例、110死亡）を紹介する教育的内容であり、新規アウトブレイクの報告ではない。豚熱（Classical Swine Fever）への言及は本文サマリーにはなく、疾患名タグの誤付与と考えられる。米国・太平洋地域も発生地域として付与されているが、記事内容と無関係のため除外。

article.articleHeadline: DCGI Clears India's First Dengue Vaccine For People Aged 4-60 Years, Offering New Tool Against Rising Disease Burden | Outlook India
article.articleSummary: India's Drug Controller General (DCGI) has cleared the country's first dengue vaccine for people aged 4–60 years, marking a milestone in India's response to rising dengue burden. In endemic regions, severe dengue remains a leading cause of hospitalization among both children and adults. The approval is expected to strengthen India's dengue prevention strategy, which has so far centered on vector-control measures such as eliminating mosquito breeding sites, insecticide spraying, surveillance, and public awareness campaigns. Health experts warn that vaccination should complement, not replace, mosquito-control efforts, since preventing mosquito breeding remains the most effective method to curb transmission. The decision introduces a new tool for reducing disease incidence and could influence future public health planning, surveillance, and vaccination campaigns across India.

article.articleHeadline: Hadapi Ancaman Zoonosis, Pemkot Surabaya Perkuat Sistem Surveilans dan Komunikasi
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Facing the Threat of Zoonosis, Surabaya City Government Strengthens the Surveillance System and Communications
article.articleSummary: Surabaya, Indonesia strengthens cross-sector preparedness for zoonotic disease threats, focusing on leptospirosis amid the rainy season. The Surabaya City Health Office (Dinkes), in collaboration with the Ministry of Health’s Communications and Public Information Bureau, Public Health Portal (Portkesmas), and the Risk Communication and Community Engagement (RCCE) Working Group, held a two-day Zoonosis Prevention Education Workshop on 21–22 July 2026 at Puskesmas Medokan Ayu. Attendees spanned multiple agencies, health units, civil society, PKK, Indonesian Red Cross, PD Pasar Surya, puskesmas, puskeswan, and media. The effort aims to bolster risk communication, community participation, and inter-agency coordination to prevent zoonoses from turning into outbreaks, especially during floods. Dinkes will issue advisories to all districts and subdistricts on flood-related disease vigilance. Emphasis on preventing leptospirosis includes wearing footwear in floodwaters and prompt hygiene after exposure, given rats as bacterial carriers in dirty, damp environments.

article.articleHeadline: В ДР Конго свыше 1 тыс. человек скончались от лихорадки Эбола
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: In the DR Congo, more than 1,000 people have died from Ebola fever.
article.articleSummary: Death toll from Ebola virus disease in the Democratic Republic of Congo has risen to 1,033, with 2,536 confirmed cases, according to authorities cited by Reuters via RIA Novosti. Two days earlier, officials reported 960 deaths. A spokesman for Russia’s Foreign Ministry announced the use of Russian vaccines to protect against the virus. The World Health Organization had, in mid-July, warned of repeated underestimation of the outbreak’s official scale. The report highlights ongoing transmission in the DRC and challenges in accurately tracking cases and fatalities during the epidemic.

article.articleHeadline: कांगो में हिंसा के बीच इबोला से जंग पर संकट, संयुक्त राष्ट्र ने जताई चिंता - Punjab Kesari
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Crisis in the fight against Ebola amid violence in Congo, United Nations expressed concern - Punjab Kesari
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) persists amid insecurity in North Kivu's Beni region. Attacks during 13-19 July killed at least 30 and wounded more than a dozen, displacing civilians and hampering aid delivery. By 20 July, national health authorities logged 2,473 confirmed Ebola cases across Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uele and Tshopo provinces. Since the May 15 declaration, the outbreak has spread to five provinces, with cross-border movement to Uganda and South Sudan fueling transmission. United Nations and partners are boosting surveillance, laboratory testing, treatment, and community engagement in affected areas. The UN reiterates calls for civilian protection and safe, unimpeded humanitarian access, stressing the protection of health workers and aid personnel to stop the outbreak.

article.articleHeadline: Έμπολα στο Κονγκό: Νεκροί περισσότεροι από 1.000 άνθρωποι
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in Congo: More than 1,000 people dead.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has caused 1,031 confirmed deaths among 2,473 cases, with at least 737 patients in isolation or hospital care, per the DRC Health Ministry update as of Monday. Dr. Jean Kaseya, director-general of Africa CDC, told a Ghana summit that the toll reflects lack of vaccines, medicines, and funding. The World Health Organization warns the epidemic's true extent could be 2–4 times higher than official counts. US CDC modeling released last month warned worst-case scenarios could approach the size of West Africa’s 2014–2016 outbreak. MSF emergency program head Trish Newport emphasized that late diagnostics have historically preceded large Ebola surges.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴでエボラ出血熱：死者1,000人超え
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国でエボラ出血熱の死者が1,000人を超え、致死率も高く国際的な支援ニーズが顕在化しており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する。
triage.notes: ガーナでのサミットはAfrica CDC責任者の発言の場であり、ガーナ国内での発生ではないためverified_locationsには含めない。米国CDCのモデリング分析も米国内発生ではないため除外。WHOは実際の感染者数が公式発表の2〜4倍の可能性を指摘しており、過小評価リスクがある。

article.articleHeadline: ईबोला महामारी फैली, 2 महीने में 1000 से ज्यादा लोगों की मौत - CNBC Awaaz
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak spreads, over 1,000 people dead in two months - CNBC Awaaz
article.articleSummary: As of 23 July 2026, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has 2,473 confirmed cases and 1,031 deaths, one of the fastest-spreading Ebola outbreaks in history. Authorities say lack of vaccines, medicines, and funding hampers response, and the current virus may differ from earlier variants. Insurgent groups and community distrust impede access for health teams, delaying interventions. Attacks on health facilities and safe-burial teams disrupt relief work, and unpaid salaries hamper care. About 80% of new infections have no clear link to previous cases, indicating rapid spread to new areas. WHO warns the outbreak could exceed official counts, underscoring an urgent need for intensified control measures.

triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で史上最速レベルのエボラ流行が進行中で、2473症例・1031死亡、8割が感染経路不明という深刻な拡大を示しており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するためフルRRAが必要。

article.articleHeadline: Congo Ebola outbreak: Death toll crosses 1,000, says Africa CDC
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in Congo has caused more than 1,000 deaths, with 1,031 confirmed, according to Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention, Africa's top health body, making it the fastest Ebola outbreak in history. As of 2026-07-23, conflict, community resistance, and an uneven response are fueling its spread. Africa CDC Director-General Dr. Jean Kaseya spoke at a health summit in Ghana. The scene accompanying the report shows health workers in protective equipment disinfecting an isolation area for Ebola patients, highlighting the ongoing crisis and strain on healthcare systems as responders attempt to curb transmission and protect communities. The report underscores the urgency of a coordinated international response.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ・エボラ流行:死者数1,000人を突破、アフリカCDCが発表

triage.notes: ガーナは会議開催地として言及されているのみで、エボラ発生国ではないため verified_locations から除外した。

article.articleHeadline: الإيبولا يواصل الانتشار.. نحو ألف وفاة مؤكدة وسط تحذيرات من تفاقم الأزمة - عكس السير
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola continues to spread... nearly 1,000 confirmed deaths amid warnings of the crisis worsening - Aks al-Sayr
article.articleSummary: Outbreak of Ebola virus in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) continues to intensify, with 999 confirmed deaths and 2,473 confirmed infections. The current surge is caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus (Bundibugyo lineage), for which there is no approved vaccine or proven treatment; clinical trials are testing promising therapies. Ongoing insecurity and limited access to affected areas hinder containment. The epidemic has also reached Uganda, reporting 20 confirmed cases and 2 deaths; authorities announced the discharge of the last patient and initiated the 42-day countdown to declare Ebola-free if no new infections occur, per WHO criteria. Health experts warn the true case count may be higher due to weak surveillance and cases in remote or conflict-affected regions, calling for a strengthened international response to prevent further spread.

article.articleHeadline: Sốt xuất huyết, tay chân miệng tăng mạnh, Lâm Đồng chỉ đạo siết chặt phòng chống dịch
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Dengue fever and hand-foot-mouth disease surge; Lam Dong Province orders stricter disease prevention and control measures.
article.articleSummary: Lam Dong Province, Vietnam reports a surge in dengue fever and hand-foot-mouth disease. From the start of 2026 through July 23, the province recorded 2,285 dengue cases, including 57 severe cases and 1 death, up 9.7% year-on-year, and 3,076 hand-foot-mouth disease cases with 2 fatalities. In response, the Provincial People’s Committee issued directive 11931/UBND-KGVX on July 23, 2026, ordering all departments, agencies, and the Phu Quy Special Zone to implement synchronized prevention and control measures. The Department of Health will monitor epidemiology, reinforce surveillance in high-risk areas and outbreaks, ensure diagnosis, treatment, referral, hospital capacity, and supply medicines, equipment, beds, and personnel; train health workers and community surveillance teams, and coordinate with media to raise awareness. Preventive actions emphasize environmental sanitation to eliminate standing water and larval habitats for dengue, hygiene for hand-foot-mouth, school outreach, and community mobilization under the '4-at-site' approach to prevent large outbreaks during the rainy season.

triage.headline_ja: デング熱・手足口病が急増、ラムドン省が感染対策の強化を指示
triage.triage_reason: ベトナム・ラムドン省での季節性のデング熱・手足口病の増加であり、地方政府が対策を強化しているが、国際的異常性・拡大リスクは低い。国内の年次流行パターンとして経過観察が妥当。
triage.notes: デング熱・手足口病はベトナムの雨季における季節性感染症であり、地方政府（ラムドン省人民委員会）が指令11931/UBND-KGVXを発出し対応強化を指示。死亡例（デング1名、手足口病2名）はあるが、例年の流行パターンの範囲内とみられ、国際的な拡大や渡航制限の懸念は記載なし。

article.articleHeadline: الكونغو الديمقراطية تشهد مؤشرات مبكرة على استقرار الإيبولا
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Democratic Republic of the Congo sees early indicators of Ebola stabilization.
article.articleSummary: EBOLA virus disease ongoing in the Democratic Republic of the Congo shows early stabilization signals in some eastern provinces, though officials warn it is premature to declare a peak. Adielard Lovongola, Operations Director for the national Ebola response, stated at a Bunia press conference that cases have entered a stabilization phase with a slight downward trend, but the outbreak remains active. Response capacity has expanded to 23 Ebola treatment centers, 19 laboratories, and about 800 beds. Ongoing challenges include community resistance, insecurity, and geographic spread; emphasis is placed on early detection, public trust in health facilities, and adherence to preventive measures to interrupt transmission chains. As of July 20, 2026, government figures report 2,473 confirmed cases, 999 deaths, 482 recoveries, and 737 patients in treatment or isolation, with the outbreak persisting in five eastern provinces since May 15.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国、エボラ出血熱の安定化を示す早期兆候
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱の大規模アウトブレイクが継続中であり、致死率約40%（999人死亡/2473人確定例）、5州にまたがる拡大、治安・コミュニティの抵抗といった不安定要素があるため、フルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 既知の継続中アウトブレイクだが、安定化の兆候はあるものの依然として活動的であり、治安不安・コミュニティの抵抗など流行拡大リスクが残る。続報でのトレンド確認が必要。

article.articleHeadline: കോംഗോയില്‍ ചരിത്രത്തിലെ തന്നെ ഏറ്റവും വേഗത്തില്‍ പടരുന്ന എബോള വ്യാപനം: മരണസംഖ്യ 1,000 കടന്നു. വാക്‌സിനുകളോ ഫലപ്രദമായ ചികിത്സയോ ഇല്ലാത്ത അപൂര്‍വ്വ 'ബുന്ദിബുഗ്യോ' വൈറസ് ജനങ്ങള്‍ക്കിടയില്‍ ഭീതി പടര്‍ത്തവേ ശമ്പള കുടിശ്ശികയെ തുടര്‍ന്ന് പ്രതിരോധത്തിലായ ആരോഗ്യപ്രവര്‍ത്തകര്‍ പണിമുടക്കിലേക്ക്, മരുന്നുകളുടെ പരീക്ഷണം ആരംഭിച്ചെങ്കിലും കലാപബാധിത മേഖലകളില്‍ പടര്‍ന്നുപിടിക്കുന്ന രോഗത്തെ നിയന്ത്രിക്കാനാവാതെ ആഗോള ആരോഗ്യ ഏജന്‍സികള്‍
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: In Congo, the fastest-spreading Ebola outbreak in history has claimed more than 1,000 lives. With no vaccines or effective treatments for the rare Bundibugyo virus, fear is spreading among people, as health workers go on strike due to salary arrears; although drug trials have begun, global health agencies are unable to contain the disease spreading in conflict-affected areas.
article.articleSummary: Eastern Congo is facing the Bundibugyo Ebola virus outbreak, described as the fastest-spreading in history, with the death toll exceeding 1,031 according to Africa CDC Director‑General Dr. Jean Kaseya. About 90% of cases are in remote areas, with five provinces affected including Kisangani. The surge occurs amid conflict, shortages of protective gear, and health workers’ strikes over salary arrears, complicating containment. Misinformation that Ebola is a hoax further impedes response. Severe symptoms include dehydration and bleeding. There are no approved vaccines or standard therapies for Bundibugyo Ebola; however, treatment trials are underway using Remdesivir and the experimental MBP134 at local centers to assess safety and efficacy. The Congo government and United Nations agencies are intensifying measures to halt transmission in this volatile, outbreak-prone region, with CDC warning of potential escalation to 2014-16 West Africa levels.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴで史上最速のエボラ流行拡大、死者1,000人超え。ワクチンや有効な治療法のない希少な「ブンディブギョ」ウイルスが人々の間に恐怖を広げる中、給与未払いを背景に医療従事者がストライキに突入。薬剤治験は開始されたが、紛争地帯での感染拡大を国際保健機関も抑制できていない。
triage.triage_reason: 史上最速拡大とされる大規模エボラ（ブンディブギョ株）流行で死者1,000人超、紛争地域での対応困難、ワクチン・治療薬未承認、国際機関が介入している点からIHR基準複数該当かつ社会的関心も高い。
triage.notes: 発生地域にAngolaが含まれるが、記事サマリーはコンゴ東部（キサンガニ含む5州）に限定して言及しており、Angolaでの発生には触れていないため除外した。CDCは2014-16西アフリカ規模への拡大の可能性を警告している。

article.articleHeadline: Dịch Ebola ở châu Phi: Số ca tử vong tăng lên hơn 1.000 người
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak in Africa: Death toll rises to more than 1,000.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in Africa continues to surge, with deaths surpassing 1,000. Data released on July 22 by health agencies in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and Uganda show 2,473 confirmed Ebola cases and 999 deaths in DRC as of July 20, with 737 patients in isolation or hospital care and 482 recoveries. Uganda reports 20 confirmed cases and 2 deaths. Africa CDC Director Jean Kaseya warns the current outbreak could become one of the worst if not rapidly controlled, calling for stronger political commitment and expanded resources to intensify coordinated health and humanitarian responses, with funding needs rising. World Health Organization Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus warned last week that the outbreak has spread faster than any prior Ebola outbreak. Despite intensified response, transmission remains complex in the DRC.

triage.headline_ja: アフリカのエボラ流行:死者数が1,000人超に増加
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱がDRCとウガンダで拡大し、死者1,000人超・過去最速の拡大速度とWHO・Africa CDCが警告しており、IHR基準・WPRO基準共に複数該当する重大な公衆衛生上のシグナルである。
triage.notes: ウガンダも罹患国として言及されているが、対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations から除外。WHO・Africa CDC共に深刻な警告を発しており、フルRRAへの移行が妥当。

article.articleHeadline: 非洲本轮伊波拉疫情死亡病例破千|光华网
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Death toll in Africa's current Ebola outbreak surpasses 1,000
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Uganda, caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, has surpassed 1,000 deaths. As of July 20, 2026 in the DRC, there are 2,473 laboratory-confirmed cases and 999 deaths; Uganda reported 20 confirmed cases and 2 deaths by July 21. Across both countries, total deaths reach 1,001. The DRC has 737 patients in isolation or hospital care and 482 recoveries. WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus noted this is the third-largest Ebola outbreak on record and that spread has accelerated in the past month. Uganda’s last patient recovered on July 16, and the country has entered a 42-day observation period; per WHO guidance, a country may declare the outbreak over after 42 days without a new confirmed case from the last patient.

triage.headline_ja: 非洲本轮伊波拉疫情死亡病例破千（アフリカの今回のエボラ出血熱流行、死者数1000人を突破）
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国とウガンダにおけるエボラ出血熱（ブンディブギョ株）の流行が死者1000人を超え、WHOも史上3番目の規模と指摘する重大な公衆衛生事象であり、国際的拡大リスクも懸念される。
triage.notes: ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations から除外。ただし越境流行であり国際的拡大リスクの根拠として言及。

article.articleHeadline: Över 1000 döda i ebola i Kongo-Kinshasa
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Over 1,000 dead from Ebola in Congo-Kinshasa.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has killed over 1,000, making it the fastest-growing outbreak in history, according to Médecins Sans Frontières. The true scale is believed to be 2–4 times higher than detected, per WHO health crisis chief Chikwe Ihekweazu (July 9, 2026). In Bunia, the outbreak’s epicenter, transmission remains intense, with 70–80% of new cases arising from people not on known contact lists. In Bunia, one of two Ebola tests conducted was positive, signaling widespread community transmission. Roughly two-thirds of deaths occur in communities where patients never receive treatment. In May, residents lived in fear as funerals could not be held normally; a late-May incident saw crowds set fire to hospital tents housing Ebola patients to reclaim bodies.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国（キンシャサ）でエボラ出血熱により1000人以上死亡
triage.triage_reason: 1000人以上の死者を伴う史上最速拡大のエボラアウトブレイクであり、コミュニティ内感染が広範化し封じ込めが困難な状況であるため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する。
triage.notes: WHOやMSFが関与し国際的な公衆衛生上の懸念が高い。地域住民の不信・暴動（病院テント放火）が発生しており、対応の困難さと感染拡大リスクが顕著。

locations.name: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

article.articleHeadline: British Airways Investigates After 3 Pilots on Flight BA276 Fall Ill Following Hyderabad Stopover
article.articleSummary: Three British Airways pilots on flight BA276 from Hyderabad to London Heathrow fell ill with suspected food poisoning after breakfast at a crew hotel in Hyderabad. One pilot became incapacitated at 30,000 feet and required oxygen; the other two’s symptoms worsened as the roughly 10.5-hour Boeing 777-200 flight continued and landed safely. Post-flight, symptoms persisted, and all three filed Air Safety Reports and provided samples to help doctors identify the illness source. The airline said passenger safety was not compromised. Investigations focus on the possible source: bottled water from an external supplier consumed at the Hyderabad hotel rather than the hotel’s water. BA is reviewing crew accommodation arrangements in Hyderabad and considering hotel options. No definitive cause has been disclosed; ongoing investigation as of 2026-07-23.

triage.headline_ja: 英国航空、BA276便のパイロット3名がハイデラバード経由後に体調不良、調査中
triage.triage_reason: 特定の航空機乗務員3名に限定された食中毒疑いの単発事例であり、公衆衛生上の広がりや異常性を示す情報がないため。
triage.notes: 食中毒（ボトル水が疑われる）による乗務員個人への健康被害であり、感染症の集団発生や公衆衛生上の脅威を示す証拠はない。航空会社の内部調査事案。

article.articleHeadline: В Африке от Эболы умерли почти 1000 человек. Вакцины от этого штамма нет
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: In Africa, nearly 1,000 people have died from Ebola. There is no vaccine for this strain.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) escalates. Laboratory-confirmed infections reach 2,473 with 999 deaths; 737 patients are in isolation. The WHO has declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern, the second-highest global risk. The virus has spread across five of the DRC’s 26 provinces (population ~116 million) and has crossed into Uganda, with 20 cases and 2 deaths reported there. The epicenter is Ituri province in the northeast, a region already strained by armed conflict. The current strain is Bundibugyo, a rare variant for which there is no licensed vaccine or specific treatment. Case fatality is estimated at 30–50%. The incubation period can reach up to three weeks, and transmission is via direct contact with bodily fluids; unsafe funeral practices fuel spread. Only 82% of contacts are traced, short of the 90% target; this marks the 17th Ebola outbreak in DRC since 1976.

triage.headline_ja: アフリカでエボラ出血熱により約1000人が死亡。この株に対するワクチンはない
triage.triage_reason: WHOがPHEICを宣言した大規模なエボラ出血熱アウトブレイクで、国境を越えてウガンダにも拡大しており、致死率が高くワクチンが存在しない稀な株であるため、フルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: ウガンダへの越境感染が報告されているが、ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations から除外した。DRCでの17回目のエボラ流行であり、紛争地域という不安定要因も存在する。

article.articleHeadline: Congo's Ebola Crisis Deepens: Death Toll Crosses 1,000, WHO Warns Actual Cases May Be Four Times Higher
article.articleSummary: On 2026-07-23, Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has killed 1,031 people and infected 2,473, with 737 in isolation or hospital treatment. The outbreak began May 15 and is spreading rapidly, described by Africa CDC Director-General Dr. Jean Kaseya as among the fastest-growing Ebola epidemics on record. WHO cautions the true number of infections may be two to four times higher than official counts. About 80% of new infections occur outside known transmission chains, indicating widespread community transmission and hindering contact tracing. Response is hampered by severe shortages of vaccines, medicines, and funds. Ebola spreads through direct contact with bodily fluids. There is no universally effective cure; vaccines and supportive treatments exist in some settings. The situation underscores the need for early detection and containment in DRC.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ危機深刻化：死者数1,000人超え、WHOは実際の感染者数は4倍に上る可能性を警告
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で急速に拡大するエボラ出血熱アウトブレイクで死者1,000人超・感染者2,473人、コミュニティ内感染が拡大し封じ込めが困難な状況であり、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する重大事案。
triage.notes: WHOはワクチン・医薬品・資金の深刻な不足を指摘。新規感染の約80％が既知の感染連鎖の外で発生しており、地域社会内感染が進行中で、史上最速級のエボラ流行との評価。フルRRAへの移行が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Health: Uganda sets up 80-bed Ebola Isolation and Treatment
article.articleSummary: Uganda has established an 80-bed Ebola isolation and treatment unit in Kasenyi, eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), with a second Ugandan team aiding response in Aru. The facility, completed by Ugandan medical teams, is designed to isolate, treat and manage patients and to curb cross-border movement of infected people into Uganda, as Kampala and Kinshasa boost cooperation after Uganda reported an imported case linked to Congo. Health Minister Dr. Chris Baryomunsi indicated Uganda remains ready to expand deployment if needed; the MOH cited an MoU signed with Congo to coordinate surveillance, treatment and outbreak response. Uganda enters the second week of a 42-day countdown to being declared Ebola-free by WHO; 35 days remain since the discharge of the last Ugandan patient on July 16 (a Congolese national). Uganda's outbreak saw 20 cases, 2 deaths (CFR ~10%). Across DRC, 2,300 cases and 930 deaths reported, with ongoing response.

triage.headline_ja: 保健:ウガンダが80床のエボラ隔離・治療施設を設置
triage.triage_reason: DRCで2,300症例・930人死亡の大規模エボラ流行が継続し、ウガンダへの越境感染例も発生しているため、国際的拡大リスクと公衆衛生への深刻な影響が認められる。
triage.notes: ウガンダは越境感染の関連国だが対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations から除外。DRCでの大規模流行（2,300症例、930死亡）が主題であり、国境をまたぐ対応（ウガンダによる隔離施設設置、MoU締結）が進行中。ウガンダは既存症例からのEbola-free宣言に向けたカウントダウン中。

article.articleHeadline: 暑假腸病毒疫情緩升！今年6例重症1死　5歲以下出現重症警訊快就醫 - 民視新聞網
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Summer vacation enterovirus outbreak on the rise! This year, 6 severe cases and 1 death; warning signs of severe illness appear in children under 5—seek medical care promptly - Minshi News Network
article.articleSummary: Taiwan reports an enterovirus outbreak during summer vacation, with 6 severe cases and 1 death. Laboratory surveillance identifies four EV-D68, one Coxsackie A4, and one Coxsackie A16; Coxsackie A6 remains the dominant community strain in the past four weeks. Week 28 (July 12–18) ED visits reached 7,534, similar to 7,442 the prior week. Children under 5 are the high-risk group; severe signs include drowsiness, altered consciousness, reduced activity, limb weakness or paralysis, persistent vomiting, and rapid breathing or tachycardia. Transmission remains ongoing as daycare centers and summer camps operate; households risk spread. Prevention emphasizes hygiene and cleaning with 500 ppm chlorine bleach and the 5-step handwashing protocol (wet, rub, rinse, dry, wipe). Seek prompt medical care at large hospitals for suspected severe illness. Nearby regions report rising enterovirus activity in Vietnam, China Mainland, Japan, Korea, Thailand, and Singapore.

triage.headline_ja: 夏休みにエンテロウイルス感染拡大！今年6例の重症例と1例の死亡、5歳未満で重症化の兆候に注意し速やかな受診を - 民視新聞網
triage.triage_reason: 台湾での流行が主題で重症例・死亡例が報告されているが、対象国（ベトナム・中国・タイ等）については『近隣地域で活動上昇』という一般的言及に留まり具体的データが不足しているため、続報を注視する。
triage.notes: 記事の主題は台湾（対象国外）における夏季エンテロウイルス流行（EV-D68、Coxsackie A6等）。ベトナム・中国・タイ・日本・韓国・シンガポールについては『近隣地域でも活動上昇』との簡潔な言及のみで、具体的な症例数や重症度データは記載されていない。

article.articleHeadline: Tuberkuloza, hepatitis, HIV... Strani radnici morat će na testiranja i provjeru cijepnog statusa - Novi list
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Tuberculosis, Hepatitis, HIV... Foreign workers will have to undergo testing and vaccination status verification - Novi List
article.articleSummary: Croatia's Health Ministry issued a decree requiring third-country nationals under visa regimes extending temporary residence to undergo a health screening for infectious diseases and to vaccinate as needed based on status. The measure targets visa-required nationals from India, Nepal, Bangladesh, Pakistan, the Philippines and Egypt seeking to extend their stay. Examinations, at public health institutes near the applicant's residence or at the Croatian Institute for Public Health, must occur within 90 days before extension submission and are arranged by the employer. The screening includes epidemiological history, physical exam, and vaccination checks; active tuberculosis, typhoid and paratyphoid carriage, and HIV, hepatitis B or C infections must be excluded. Those under 35 lacking vaccines for measles, polio, diphtheria and tetanus must be re-immunized; healthcare workers require hepatitis B vaccination. A certificate is issued and must be kept and shown on request. Costs: employers fund foreign-worker exams; others pay; vaccination costs are funded by HZZO. Implemented by HZJZ and county institutes.

triage.headline_ja: 結核、肝炎、HIV...外国人労働者は検査とワクチン接種状況の確認を受けなければならない - Novi List
triage.triage_reason: クロアチアが外国人労働者向けに健康診断・ワクチン接種確認を義務化する行政措置の記事であり、感染症のアウトブレイクや異常な公衆衛生事象を報告するものではない。
triage.notes: 記事はクロアチア国内の移民労働者向け健康スクリーニング規制についての内容であり、インド・ネパール・バングラデシュ・パキスタン・フィリピン・エジプトは対象者の出身国として言及されているのみで、これらの国での感染症発生を報じるものではないため、verified_locationsには含めない。

article.articleHeadline: Molekulare Diagnostik: PCR-Test zum Nachweis des Ebola-Bundibugyo-Virus entwickelt
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Molecular Diagnostics: PCR test developed for the detection of Bundibugyo ebolavirus.
article.articleSummary: PCR test for Bundibugyo virus developed by Roche Diagnostics via TIB Molbiol adds to Roche’s rapid-response molecular diagnostics platform. The assay targets Bundibugyo ebolavirus (BDBV) and is for research use only, not diagnostic use. TIB Molbiol maintains a Rapid-Response library with ~15,000 prepared designs and >3,000 positive controls, enabling swift evaluation of primer–probe combos. Performance was assessed on real clinical samples through an independent reference-lab network, with real-time feedback guiding deployment. Roche aims to bring PCR capacity closer to outbreak areas in Africa, aligning with WHO recommendations and leveraging local partnerships. Ebola is a severe filovirus disease with about 50% average fatality (25–90% range); Bundibugyo outbreaks were first documented in 1976 in Nzara (South Sudan) and Yambuku (DRC).

triage.headline_ja: 分子診断：エボラ・ブンディブギョウイルス検出用PCR検査が開発される
triage.triage_reason: エボラウイルス（ブンディブギョウ株）の診断ツール開発に関する記事で、新規アウトブレイク報告ではなく技術開発記事である。DRCはエボラ流行地域として言及されているが、現在のアクティブな流行イベント報告ではないため、情報不足の状態で経過観察が適切。
triage.notes: 本記事はRoche Diagnosticsがエボラ・ブンディブギョウ株検出用PCR検査を開発したことを報じる技術開発記事である。アクティブなアウトブレイク報告ではなく、過去のアウトブレイク事例（1976年南スーダンとDRC）への言及であるため、現在の感染症イベント兆候としてはシグナル化されない。ただし、アフリカ地域でのエボラ流行準備としてのツール整備として、今後のイベント情報更新を注視する価値あり。

article.articleHeadline: US Issues Chikungunya Travel Alert: Is India on the List? Symptoms and Safety Tips
article.articleSummary: Chikungunya outbreaks are active in multiple international destinations per the US CDC travel alert dated 2026-07-23. The listed locations are Costa Rica, Bolivia, French Guiana, Mauritius, Mayotte, Seychelles, and Suriname. In Costa Rica, authorities have intensified mosquito-control efforts, fumigating thousands of homes, eliminating breeding sites, and investigating suspected infections after confirming multiple chikungunya cases. The article focuses on ongoing outbreaks and travel considerations for U.S. travelers, noting only that multiple cases have been confirmed in Costa Rica and providing no exact counts or incubation details. The piece references a question in the title about India's inclusion on the list, but it does not confirm any Indian outbreak status in the body.

triage.headline_ja: 米国がチクングニア熱の渡航警報を発令：インドはリストに入っているか？症状と安全対策
triage.triage_reason: 記事は米国CDCの渡航警報に基づき、コスタリカ等での chikungunya流行を扱っているが、対象国（インド含む）での確定発生は本文で否定されており、対象国に関する具体的シグナルはない。
triage.notes: 記事タイトルではインドの状況が疑問形で提示されているが、本文ではインドでの流行は確認されていないと明記されている。対象国リストに該当する確定発生国はなし。

article.articleHeadline: Swine Flu Alert In Nagpur: Cases Rise To 15 In July, One Dead
article.articleSummary: Nagpur records 25 swine flu (H1N1) cases and one death this year, with 15 infections in July alone, of which 13 were in the city limits. Authorities have stepped up surveillance: Nagpur Municipal Corporation directs the Health Department to place the division on high alert, monitor flu-like illnesses and severe respiratory infections, track daily cases, keep essential medicines stocked, and perform clinical audits of every H1N1 death to refine treatment strategies. Because of rising seasonal influenza activity, the Nagpur division escalates monitoring for influenza-like illness (ILI) and severe acute respiratory infection (SARI). Citizens are urged to watch for fever, severe cough, cold, sore throat and breathing difficulties; high-risk groups: seniors, children under five, pregnant women, and those with weakened immunity or chronic conditions should seek immediate care. Early diagnosis and timely treatment are emphasized to keep H1N1 manageable.

triage.headline_ja: ナグプールで豚インフルエンザ警報：7月の症例が15件に増加、1人死亡
triage.triage_reason: 季節性H1N1（豚インフルエンザ）の症例増加であり既知の疾患だが、当局が監視強化を行っている段階であり、今後の推移を注視する必要がある。
triage.notes: 季節性インフルエンザ（H1N1）の地域的増加であり、当局は既に監視・臨床対応を強化している。国際的な拡大リスクは低いが、症例数の推移と死亡例の増加を継続的に確認する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: কলকাতায় ভয়াবহ রূপ নিচ্ছে কোভিড! ৮ জন আক্রান্ত হতেই ফুসফুস বিশেষজ্ঞদের জরুরি অ্যালার্ট
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: COVID is taking a terrifying turn in Kolkata! Pulmonologists issue an urgent alert as soon as eight people are infected.
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-07-23, Kolkata reports eight COVID-19 infections, with pulmonologists issuing an urgent alert. Preventive guidance emphasizes: wear N-95 or good surgical masks in crowded spaces (local trains, buses, metro, malls); wash hands with soap for 20 seconds or use alcohol-based sanitizer; avoid crowds and maintain 3–6 feet distance; do not touch eyes, nose, or mouth; cover coughs or sneezes with tissue or elbow and dispose properly. If fever, cold, cough, sore throat, or body aches occur, isolate and promptly test for COVID-19. Boost immunity with vitamin-C rich foods, fresh vegetables, and hydration; ensure ventilation by opening windows. If not vaccinated or booster doses, follow a doctor's advice to receive them. Seek medical care if symptoms worsen. Measures aim to enable early detection and reduce transmission in Kolkata.

triage.headline_ja: コルカタでCOVIDが深刻化！8人感染で肺専門医が緊急警戒
triage.triage_reason: 感染者8人という小規模な事例であり、COVID-19自体は既知の疾患で新規性・異常性がなく、通常の予防啓発記事にとどまるため取り上げ基準に該当しない。
triage.notes: 既知の疾患COVID-19の小規模感染に関する予防啓発記事であり、シグナルとしての重要性は低い。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola en RDC et en Ouganda : le cap des 1 000 décès franchi, selon l'OMS
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in the DRC and Uganda: the 1,000-death milestone reached, according to the WHO.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreaks in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Uganda have surpassed 1,000 deaths, per the World Health Organization. As of July 20, DRC recorded 999 deaths; Uganda added two, bringing the total to 1,001. In the DRC, community transmission persists across five provinces, with Ituri province as the epicenter reporting 2,202 confirmed cases and 838 deaths. Since the declaration of the 17th Ebola outbreak in the DRC, the country has logged 2,473 lab-confirmed cases and more than 500 recoveries. The WHO also announced the first safety trial of the ChAdOx1 vaccine, conducted by the University of Oxford in the United Kingdom. Data reflect ongoing transmission and vaccination research as of July 22, 2026.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国とウガンダのエボラ出血熱、WHOによれば死者数1,000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱によりDRCとウガンダで死者1,000人超、コミュニティ感染が5州で継続しており、国際的拡大リスクと重大な公衆衛生影響がある。
triage.notes: ウガンダも影響を受けているが対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めない。ワクチン安全性試験（ChAdOx1）が英国オックスフォード大学で開始されているが、これは対象国の発生事象ではない。

article.articleHeadline: وفيات "إيبولا" في أفريقيا تتجاوز 1000 حالة والإصابات ترتفع
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola deaths in Africa exceed 1,000 as infections rise.
article.articleSummary: As of July 20, 2026, Ebola deaths in Africa have surpassed 1,000, with total fatalities reaching 1,001 in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Uganda. The DRC reports 2,473 confirmed cases, including 999 deaths, while Uganda records 20 cases and 2 deaths. Together, the two countries have 2,493 confirmed infections since the outbreak was first declared in eastern DRC on May 15, and the virus has spread to four additional provinces. Ongoing clinical management includes 737 patients under treatment or in isolation, and 482 people have recovered. The figures highlight continued transmission and response efforts in the affected nations as authorities monitor the evolving outbreak.

triage.headline_ja: アフリカでのエボラ出血熱による死者が1,000人を超え、感染者数も増加
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国とウガンダにまたがるエボラ出血熱の大規模流行で、死者1,000人超・感染者2,493人に達し、複数州へ拡大していることからIHR基準を複数満たす。
triage.notes: ウガンダも感染確認国だが対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsから除外。DRCが主要な発生地であり継続的な監視が必要。

article.articleHeadline: 콩고 에볼라 사망자 1000명 넘었다... "역대 가장 빠른 확산" 비상 - 월간조선
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola deaths in Congo surpass 1,000... "fastest spread in history" emergency - Monthly Chosun
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed 1,000 deaths, with 1,031 fatalities and 2,473 infections reported as of July 20; at least 737 patients were isolated or hospitalized. Declared May 15, the outbreak is due to Bundibugyo virus, for which no approved vaccine or treatment exists. It is centered in eastern DRC’s Ituri Province, where ongoing armed conflict hampers surveillance and vaccination efforts. Community resistance to burial teams, shortages of equipment and staff, and security incidents impede response; some aid workers have left or not received pay, and teams have been attacked. WHO says the outbreak could be 2–4 times larger than official counts; CDC modeling warns it could approach the scale of 2014–2016, though some experts doubt that. About 80% of new infections occur outside known transmission chains, and more than 60% of deaths occur before treatment; only ~9% of contacts are currently managed.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ・エボラ死者1000人超え…「史上最速の拡散」非常事態
triage.triage_reason: DRCでのエボラ（ブンディブギョウイルス）流行が1,000人以上の死者を出し、承認されたワクチン・治療法がなく、武力紛争により対応が阻害され国際的拡大リスクが高いため、IHR基準複数該当かつ社会的関心も高い。
triage.notes: WHOは実際の感染規模が公式発表の2〜4倍に達する可能性を指摘。CDCモデリングでは2014-2016年規模に接近する恐れがあるとされるが、専門家の間で意見が分かれている。承認されたワクチン・治療薬が存在しないブンディブギョウイルス株である点も懸念材料。

article.articleHeadline: La RD del Congo supera la barrera de los 1.000 muertos confirmados por el brote de ébola
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Democratic Republic of the Congo surpasses 1,000 confirmed deaths in the Ebola outbreak.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed 1,000 fatalities. As of July 21, the INSP reports 2,536 confirmed cases and 1,033 deaths (case fatality 40.7%). About 738 people remain in isolation or hospital, and 506 have recovered; contact tracing stands at 77.2%. Five provinces are affected: Ituri (epicenter), North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uele, and Tshopo. Officials warn that contact-tracing results remain insufficient, requiring stronger surveillance. Declared May 15 in Ituri near borders with Sudan and Uganda, the outbreak has spread to Uganda, which recorded 20 cases (15 imported from DRC) and two deaths; a 42-day countdown has begun. The outbreak is caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, with a case fatality roughly 30–50%; no approved vaccine or specific treatment exists. This is the third-worst Ebola epidemic on record and the seventeenth in DRC. Transmission is via contact with bodily fluids; symptoms include fever, vomiting, diarrhea, and bleeding.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国、エボラ出血熱流行で死者1,000人の大台を突破
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱の大規模流行で死者1,000人超・致死率40.7%に達し、ウガンダへの越境拡大も確認されており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する重大シグナル。
triage.notes: ウガンダへの感染拡大も報告されているが、対象国リストにウガンダは含まれないためverified_locationsには含めていない。DRCにおける歴代17回目、史上3番目に深刻な流行とされる重大事案。

article.articleHeadline: India sends medical assistance to Kenya to strengthen preparedness for Ebola
article.articleSummary: India on 23 July 2026 handed over the first tranche of medical assistance weighing 4.5 tonnes to Kenya to bolster Ebola Virus Disease preparedness and broader pandemic readiness. At Nairobi’s Jomo Kenyatta International Airport, Indian High Commissioner Adarsh Swaika delivered 279 packages of PPE, sample-transport kits, infrared thermometers, face shields, protective boots and other infection-prevention materials to Kenya’s Cabinet Secretary for Health Aden Duale. A second tranche will follow soon. The aid aims to strengthen Kenya National Public Health Institute and frontline public health institutions, boosting disease surveillance, safe sample collection and transport, infection prevention and control, and protection of frontline healthcare personnel to detect, contain and respond to Ebola and other emerging diseases. This builds on over 45 tonnes of prior India-Africa CDC shipments in May-June 2026, reflecting India's ongoing health partnership with Kenya, including COVID-19 vaccine support and medical equipment grants.

triage.headline_ja: インド、エボラ対策強化のためケニアに医療支援を提供
triage.triage_reason: 本記事はケニアにおけるエボラ対策準備のためのインドからの医療支援提供に関する報道であり、実際の感染症発生・アウトブレイクの報告ではない。
triage.notes: 記事はエボラの実際の発生事例ではなく、インドからケニアへの医療物資支援（準備強化目的）に関する内容。ケニアは対象国リストに含まれず、インドも発生国ではなく支援提供国であるためverified_locationsは空とした。

article.articleHeadline: Pemkot Pekalongan Luncurkan Active Case Finding Tuberkulosis Sasar 1.350 Warga
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Pekalongan City Government Launches Active Case Finding for Tuberculosis Targeting 1,350 Residents.
article.articleSummary: Pekalongan City Government launched Active Case Finding (ACF) for Tuberculosis (TB) to curb transmission. The program targets 1,350 residents at risk or close contacts across Pekalongan. Through field outreach (jemput bola), health workers from Puskesmas and related agencies will screen residents for TB symptoms and conduct supporting diagnostic tests to confirm cases, enabling early treatment. The initiative focuses on vulnerable groups, including those with close contact to active TB patients and residents in crowded settings, and those with health conditions increasing susceptibility to pulmonary TB. This launch supports the city's commitment to national TB elimination goals by identifying cases earlier, improving treatment success, and reducing mortality. Residents are urged to cooperate and not fear screening, as TB is curable with timely, routine treatment.

triage.headline_ja: プカロンガン市政府、結核の積極的症例発見プログラムを開始、住民1,350人を対象
triage.triage_reason: 既存の結核対策プログラムの通常実施報告であり、異常な流行や公衆衛生上の緊急性を示す内容ではない。
triage.notes: 結核は既知の風土病であり、本記事は国の結核撲滅目標達成に向けた通常の症例発見活動を報じたものでシグナルには該当しない。

article.articleHeadline: Viral di Medsos Pelajar di Sidoarjo Terpapar HIV Capai 522 Orang, Dinkes: Tidak Sesuai Data Resmi
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: HIV Exposure Among Students in Sidoarjo Goes Viral on Social Media, Reaches 522 People; Health Office: Figures Do Not Match Official Data
article.articleSummary: Social media alleges 522 students in Sidoarjo were exposed to HIV/AIDS; the Health Office disputes this as inconsistent with official data. Cumulative HIV cases in 11–17-year-olds from 2001–2026 total 60, with 7 deaths; 53 youths living with HIV. This is 25-year accumulated, not yearly new cases. Among 0–10-year-olds, 117 cases exist, including 35 deaths and 50 lost to follow-up; 32 currently receive antiretroviral therapy. Most early-child infections arise from mother-to-child transmission. Authorities caution against unverified posts. Delta Crisis Center data differ due to coverage. For students and older youths, emphasis on education, psychosocial support, stigma reduction, and maintaining access to schooling is stressed. Figures current as of July 2026 (published July 23, 2026).

triage.headline_ja: シドアルジョの生徒がHIVに感染したとSNSで拡散、522人に達すると主張も保健局は公式データと不一致と反論
triage.triage_reason: SNS上の噂に対する保健局の訂正報道であり、25年間の累積データに基づくもので新規アウトブレイクではなく、国際的拡大や公衆衛生上の緊急性は認められない。
triage.notes: 記事はSNSで拡散した誤情報を保健局が公式データで訂正する内容。HIV/AIDSは既知の風土病であり新規シグナルとしての緊急性は低い。

article.articleHeadline: ഹൈദരാബാദിൽ നിന്ന് ലണ്ടനിലേക്ക് പറന്ന വിമാനത്തിലെ പൈലറ്റുമാർക്ക് ഭക്ഷ്യവിഷബാധ; അന്വേഷണം ആരംഭിച്ചു
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Food poisoning among the pilots of the Hyderabad-to-London flight; investigation has begun.
article.articleSummary: British Airways has launched an investigation into food poisoning affecting three pilots aboard BA276, the Hyderabad-to-London flight that departed from Hyderabad and landed at London Heathrow. The incident occurred about 30,000 feet in the air, with one pilot developing severe symptoms requiring in-flight oxygen; the other two experienced similar illness but landed safely. The trio reportedly ate breakfast together at a Hyderabad hotel, and also drank bottled water supplied by an external vendor, prompting investigators to probe these items as possible contamination sources. As of July 23, 2026, lab samples from the crew have been sent for testing, and the airline has reviewed crew accommodations and hotel arrangements in Hyderabad as part of ongoing welfare measures. The airline stated no passenger safety compromises and has filed an Air Safety Report; the investigation is ongoing.

triage.headline_ja: ハイデラバード発ロンドン行き便のパイロットが食中毒；調査開始
triage.triage_reason: 個別の食中毒事案であり、公衆衛生上の広がりや異常性は認められず、感染症としての国際的拡大リスクも低い。
triage.notes: 食中毒（食品由来の非感染性または個別的な事例）であり、感染症のヒト-ヒト感染や公衆衛生上の緊急性は認められない。3名の限定的な事例で航空会社が内部調査中。

article.articleHeadline: COVID-19 Risk in Telangana? Experts Issue Warning to Public
article.articleSummary: Telangana (Hyderabad) faces no confirmed COVID-19 surge yet, but experts warn of possible rise after fresh cases and COVID-related deaths reported in neighboring Andhra Pradesh. There is currently no evidence of community transmission in Telangana; authorities continue monitoring the situation. Health professionals urge vigilance and prompt medical evaluation for respiratory symptoms, noting that symptoms such as persistent cough, sore throat, body aches, severe fatigue, or fever for two or more days warrant consult with a physician. Distinguishing COVID-19 from seasonal influenza remains difficult during changing weather, and Telangana has seen an uptick in seasonal viral fevers and respiratory illnesses. Preventive measures include mask-wearing, avoiding crowded indoor spaces, and hand hygiene; those who are unwell should avoid unnecessary public outings. Vulnerable groups (elderly, pregnant women, and people with chronic conditions) should seek medical advice if symptoms develop.

triage.headline_ja: テランガナ州でCOVID-19リスク？専門家が市民に警告
triage.triage_reason: テランガナ州では感染急増や市中感染の確証はないが、隣接するアンドラプラデシュ州での症例・死亡例報告を受け専門家が注意喚起しており、続報を注視する必要がある。
triage.notes: COVID-19の季節性流行に関する注意喚起記事であり、確定的な感染急増や異常事態は報告されていない。近隣州（アンドラプラデシュ）の状況次第で今後の展開を注視する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: India Approves QDENGA, Its First Dengue Vaccine Against All 4 Serotypes
article.articleSummary: India’s CDSCO approved QDENGA (TAK-003), Takeda’s live-attenuated tetravalent dengue vaccine, marking India’s first dengue vaccine authorization. Approved for ages 4–60, it requires no prior dengue infection testing and is given as two subcutaneous doses 3 months apart. QDENGA targets all four dengue serotypes (DENV-1–DENV-4) using a DENV-2 backbone with recombinant components, designed for balanced protection and favorable safety. The decision is supported by Phase III DEN-301/TIDES data from over 20,000 children and adolescents across eight dengue-endemic countries, with ~4.5 years of follow-up showing sustained reductions in infections and severe dengue, including protection in previously exposed individuals. Lancet Global Health reports, along with WHO position papers, note practical advantages for programmatic use. Authorities emphasize vaccination will complement, not replace, vector control, surveillance, and prompt treatment in India, where dengue burden is among the world’s highest, driven by urbanization and climate change.

triage.headline_ja: インドがQDENGAを承認、全4血清型に対応する初のデング熱ワクチン
triage.triage_reason: ワクチン承認に関する規制ニュースであり、感染症アウトブレイクや異常事態を報告するものではないため、シグナルとしての緊急性はない。
triage.notes: 記事はデング熱ワクチンの承認という公衆衛生上のポジティブな進展を報じており、アウトブレイク発生や異常な感染事象を示すものではない。

locations.name: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

article.articleHeadline: Health worker monitored for Ebola in London hospital after working in DRC
article.articleSummary: On 23 July 2026, the UK Health Security Agency reported a UK resident who treated Ebola patients in the Democratic Republic of the Congo was evacuated to London on a chartered flight as a precautionary measure. The individual is asymptomatic and being monitored in isolation by infectious disease specialists while the 2–21 day Ebola incubation period passes. There are no confirmed Ebola cases in the UK, and public risk remains low. A Glasgow hospital previously treated a patient suspected of Ebola who tested negative. WHO declared the May 2026 Ebola outbreaks in the DRC and Uganda a public health emergency of international concern. Ebola transmission occurs from wildlife to humans and between people via blood and bodily fluids or contaminated surfaces; symptoms include fever, fatigue, malaise, muscle pain, headache, sore throat, vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain, rash, and kidney/liver impairment.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国での勤務後、ロンドンの病院でエボラ出血熱の経過観察を受ける医療従事者
triage.triage_reason: WHOがDRC・ウガンダのエボラ流行をPHEICと宣言しており、国際的な感染拡大（英国での経過観察事例）も確認されているため、IHR基準複数該当としてフルRRAへ進める。
triage.notes: 記事は英国での経過観察事例が主だが、根本的な流行はDRC（およびウガンダ、対象国外）で発生しWHOがPHEICを宣言済み。ウガンダ・英国は対象国リスト外のため除外。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola: Judith Suminwa conduit une mission mixte dans les provinces de la Tshopo et de l'Ituri pour renforcer la riposte
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola: Judith Suminwa leads a joint mission in the Tshopo and Ituri provinces to bolster the response.
article.articleSummary: Prime Minister Judith Suminwa leads a high-level joint mission to Kisangani in Tshopo Province, then to Bunia, Mongbwalu, and Rwampara in Ituri Province, to bolster the Ebola response in the Democratic Republic of Congo. Initiated July 23, 2026, the mission comes two months after the official declaration of the 17th Ebola outbreak, and convenes U.S. representatives, UN system partners, and technical-financial actors to assess ground realities and strengthen prevention, epidemiological surveillance, and patient care. The government aims to reaffirm leadership, accelerate a coordinated and rapid response, and protect communities while supporting frontline health workers. Ongoing challenges include security constraints and attacks on treatment centers by armed groups, alongside strikes over pay and working conditions. As of July 20, the outbreak had 999 deaths, with transmission centered in Ituri.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ:スミンワ首相、対応強化のためチョポ州とイトゥリ州で合同ミッションを実施
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国における第17次エボラ流行が継続中で、死者999人に達し、首相主導の合同対応ミッションが実施されるなど公衆衛生上・社会政治上の重大な懸念があるため。
triage.notes: 発生地域にRwandaのKigali州が含まれるが、記事サマリーではDRC国内（チョポ州・イトゥリ州）のみが対応ミッションの対象であり、Rwandaでの発生は言及されていないため除外。武装勢力による治療センターへの攻撃や医療従事者のストライキなど、対応の障害要因も存在。

article.articleHeadline: Lâm Đồng: Khẩn trương phòng chống bệnh dịch sốt xuất huyết, tay chân miệng
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Lam Dong Province: Urgent measures to prevent and control dengue fever and hand, foot and mouth disease.
article.articleSummary: Lam Dong Province, Vietnam reports 2,285 dengue fever cases in 2026 (up 9.7% year-on-year) with 57 severe cases and 1 death; Hand, Foot and Mouth Disease (HFMD) totals 3,076 cases (up 1,622) and 2 deaths, both in Ta Nang commune. Warmer, favorable conditions for mosquitoes and ongoing HFMD transmission across multiple localities raise the risk of a wider outbreak, particularly in preschools and communities. On July 23, 2026, Chairman Ho Van Muoi directed the entire political system and health authorities to institute urgent, coordinated prevention and control measures to prevent spread and safeguard public health. The Department of Health should enhance epidemiological surveillance, monitor trends, forecast risk, and rigorously document all cases, addressing old and new outbreaks; ensure adequate beds, staff, medicines, chemicals, and equipment; optimize triage and admission to minimize severe cases and fatalities. Public and private facilities must follow MOH guidelines and facilitate timely referrals.

triage.headline_ja: ラムドン省：デング熱・手足口病の予防対策を緊急実施
triage.triage_reason: ベトナム・ラムドン省での季節性デング熱と手足口病(HFMD)の症例増加であり、地方レベルの公衆衛生対応事案。国際的拡大リスクは低いが、症例数増加傾向は継続監視が必要。
triage.notes: 毎年繰り返される季節性のデング熱・HFMD流行で、前年比増加が見られるが国際的な緊急事態には該当しない。地方政府（省レベル）が予防対策を指示している段階であり、外部支援の必要性は明記されていない。続報でさらなる拡大や重症化が確認されればPICKUPへの引き上げを検討。

article.articleHeadline: Африкада Эболадан мыңға жуық адам қайтыс болды: бұл штамға қарсы вакцина жоқ
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: In Africa, nearly a thousand people died from Ebola: there is no vaccine against this strain.
article.articleSummary: The World Health Organization declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern over an Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. As of July 23, 2026, there are 2,473 laboratory-confirmed cases and 999 deaths, with 737 patients in isolation. The outbreak, which began in May, is driven by the rare Bundibugyo Ebola strain for which there is no approved vaccine or specific treatment. The virus has spread to 5 of the DRC’s 26 provinces in a country of about 116 million people and has reached neighboring Uganda, with 20 cases and 2 deaths. The epicenter is Ituri Province in the northeast, where ongoing armed conflict hampers response and unsafe burial practices may cause up to 17 secondary infections from a single death. Incubation can be up to three weeks; only 82% of contacts are monitored, short of the 90% target to halt transmission. This marks the 17th Ebola outbreak in the DRC since 1976.

triage.headline_ja: アフリカでエボラにより約1000人が死亡：この株に対するワクチンは存在しない
triage.triage_reason: WHOがコンゴ民主共和国のエボラ流行に対しPHEICを宣言し、999人の死亡と近隣ウガンダへの越境拡大が確認されているため、フルRRAへの移行が必要。
triage.notes: ウガンダへの感染拡大が報告されているが、ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めていない。武装紛争により対応が困難であり、接触者追跡率も目標(90%)未達（82%）で、今後さらなる拡大の懸念あり。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola deaths surpass 1,000 as Africa races to contain fastest-growing outbreak
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), centered in Ituri Province, has surpassed 1,000 deaths with 2,536 confirmed cases and 1,033 fatalities as of 2026-07-23, the fastest-growing epidemic on record. The outbreak is spreading beyond its original epicentre, with 17 of 34 recent deaths occurring in communities rather than treatment centres, underscoring surveillance gaps. WHO and Africa CDC warn the outbreak remains ahead of response, with health workers still behind the pace despite expanded treatment centres and safe burial teams. Experts estimate true infections may be two to four times higher than reported, with about 80% of new cases detected outside monitored contact lists. There is no vaccine for the Bundibugyo Ebola strain; control relies on surveillance, isolation and supportive care. UN warns that spread to Rwanda or Angola could push Africa losses to $3.6B in GDP and 328,000 jobs; confined to DRC/Uganda could cost about $1B.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ死者数1,000人超、アフリカが史上最速拡大のアウトブレイク封じ込めに奔走
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国でエボラ出血熱（ブンディブギョ株、ワクチンなし）が2,536症例・1,033死亡と急拡大し、地域社会への伝播や近隣国への波及リスクが高く、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するためフルRRAへ移行すべき。
triage.notes: ウガンダ・ルワンダ・アンゴラは経済的波及リスクとして言及されているのみで、実際の症例発生は確認されていないため verified_locations には含めていない。ワクチンが存在しないブンディブギョ株であること、症例の約8割が接触者リスト外で検出されていることから、サーベイランスの限界と急速な地域社会内伝播が強く懸念される。

article.articleHeadline: وفيات 'إيبولا' في إفريقيا تتجاوز ألف حالة والإصابات ترتفع إلى 2493
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola deaths in Africa exceed 1,000, and infections rise to 2,493.
article.articleSummary: Ebola deaths in Africa exceed 1,000 as infections rise to 2,493, centered in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda. By July 20, the DRC reported 2,473 confirmed cases and 999 deaths; Uganda logged 20 cases and 2 deaths. Total confirmed infections reach 2,493 and deaths 1,001 since the outbreak began on May 15 in eastern DRC, with spread to four more provinces. Ongoing clinical management includes 737 patients under treatment or in isolation, and 482 recoveries. The figures underscore a sustained Ebola outbreak in Central and East Africa, with public health authorities continuing surveillance and containment efforts. The data reflect laboratory-confirmed results and ongoing outbreak response across affected districts and health zones.

triage.headline_ja: アフリカでのエボラ死者数が1000人を超え、感染者数は2,493人に増加
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国を中心に感染者2,493人・死者1,001人に達する大規模エボラアウトブレイクであり、複数州への拡大とウガンダへの越境伝播が確認されているため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する。
triage.notes: 記事はDRCとウガンダでの感染状況を報告しているが、ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations から除外。モザンビークは発生地域リストにあるが記事本文に言及がないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: RD Kongo tunjukkan tanda-tanda awal stabilisasi wabah ebola
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: DR Congo shows early signs of stabilization of the Ebola outbreak.
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo strain of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo shows early signs of stabilization across five eastern provinces, with Bunia in Ituri Province a focal point. As of 20 July 2026, the DRC has reported 2,473 confirmed cases, 999 deaths, 482 recoveries, and 737 patients still in isolation or hospital. Officials say case reporting has entered a stabilization phase with a slight downward trend, though it is too early to declare a peak. Response capacity has expanded to 23 Ebola treatment centers, 19 operational laboratories, and nearly 800 beds in affected areas. Ongoing challenges include community resistance, security vulnerabilities, and geographic spread. Emphasis remains on early detection, public trust in health facilities, and adherence to prevention measures to interrupt transmission. The outbreak was announced on May 15 in eastern DRC."

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国、エボラ出血熱流行の初期安定化の兆候を示す
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国東部での大規模なエボラ出血熱流行（2,473症例、999死亡）が継続しており、地理的拡大や地域社会の抵抗などの課題も残るため、フルリスク評価が必要と判断される。
triage.notes: 致死率は約40%と高く、5つの東部州にまたがる流行。地域社会の抵抗、治安の脆弱性、地理的拡大が継続課題として挙げられており、安定化の兆候はあるもののピークアウト宣言には時期尚早とされている。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola Death Toll In The Democratic Republic Of Congo Surges Above 1,000
article.articleSummary: DRC’s latest Ebola outbreak, caused by the Bundibugyo strain, has killed 1,031 people and infected 2,473 confirmed cases since it emerged in May in Ituri province, making it the fastest-spreading Ebola outbreak on record. About 737 patients are currently in isolation or hospitalized. Bundibugyo is a rare human Ebola variant with no approved vaccines or treatments. WHO incident manager Thierno Balde said the outbreak remains ahead of containment. Two deaths have also been reported in neighboring Uganda; Uganda’s last Ebola patient was discharged on July 16, initiating a 42-day countdown to be declared free of the virus per WHO guidelines. Africa CDC Director-General Jean Kaseya urged urgent action and discussed lifting Uganda travel restrictions; the U.S. maintains entry bans for travelers recently in DRC, Uganda, or South Sudan. The outbreak was declared May 15.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ死者数、1,000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: ワクチン・治療法未承認の希少株による過去最速拡大のエボラ流行で、死者1,000人超・隣国ウガンダへの越境事例も確認され、渡航制限も発生しているためIHR基準を複数満たす。
triage.notes: ウガンダでも2名の死亡例が報告されているが、対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めていない。米国は対象国リスト外のため除外。

article.articleHeadline: Dinkes Sidoarjo Klarifikasi Kabar 522 Pelajar Positif HIV/AIDS
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Sidoarjo Health Office Clarifies Report of 522 Students Testing Positive for HIV/AIDS
article.articleSummary: Sidoarjo Regency Health Office in East Java, Indonesia, debunks a social-media claim that 522 students tested positive for HIV/AIDS. Official data as of 23 July 2026 show 60 students aged 11–17 diagnosed with HIV/AIDS since 2001, with 7 deaths and 53 survivors. In the 0–10 age group, 117 children have been infected since 2001, including 35 deaths and 50 lost to follow-up; 32 children remain on antiretroviral therapy. The Health Office says the 522 figure is false and urges reliance on government data to prevent stigma. The clarification occurred during a joint event with Yayasan Delta Crisis Center in Sidoarjo. No details on transmission sources or laboratory confirmation are provided, underscoring data management rather than an active outbreak.

triage.headline_ja: スィドアルジョ保健局、522人の学生がHIV/AIDS陽性という報道を否定
triage.triage_reason: SNS上の誤情報（522人陽性）を保健当局が公式データで否定した記事であり、2001年以降の累積既知症例数の説明にとどまる。新規アウトブレイクや異常事態ではない。
triage.notes: 記事の主眼はSNS上の誤情報に対する保健局の訂正であり、HIV/AIDSは既知の慢性感染症で新規の公衆衛生上の脅威を示すものではない。感染経路や検査確認の詳細も不明。

article.articleHeadline: Public support key weapon in fight against dengue: Civil Surgeon at Janata Nagar camp - The Tribune
article.articleSummary: Public support is key in dengue fight in Ludhiana district, Janata Nagar. Civil Surgeon Dr Ramandeep Kaur told a dengue awareness camp that Aedes aegypti mosquitoes breeding in clean, stagnant water around homes—water in coolers, refrigerator trays, flower pots, discarded tyres, utensils on rooftops, overhead tanks—drive transmission. Officials urged weekly inspection and drainage of stagnant water, covering water containers, and maintaining household cleanliness as essential to dengue prevention. Since bites occur during the day, residents were advised to wear full-sleeve clothing and seek immediate care at government health facilities for fever, avoiding self-medication. The anti-larva wing conducted door-to-door inspections for larvae surveillance, distributed pamphlets, and urged residents to drain water promptly. The effort aims to make Ludhiana a dengue-free district through shared responsibility and community participation.

triage.headline_ja: デング熱との闘いにおいて住民の協力が鍵：ジャナタ・ナガル・キャンプでの民間外科医の発言
triage.triage_reason: デング熱に関する日常的な予防啓発活動の報道であり、異常な発生状況や重症化・拡大の兆候は記載されていない。
triage.notes: デング熱の季節的な予防啓発キャンペーンに関する記事であり、具体的な症例数や流行状況の記載はない。

article.articleHeadline: Dinkes Gorontalo Respons Cepat KLB Campak di Desa Dudepo Kepulauan
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Gorontalo Health Office Responds Quickly to Measles Outbreak in Dudepo Village, Kepulauan Islands
article.articleSummary: Measles outbreak declared in Dudepo Village, Kepulauan Islands, Gorontalo Province, Indonesia, prompting a rapid response by the Gorontalo Health Office. With KLB (Kejadian Luar biasa) status established, health teams conduct epidemiological investigations, secure medical logistics, and provide additional vaccination for vulnerable groups. Measures include mass screening of residents, outbreak response immunization for children, and community education on hygiene and early symptoms to prompt reporting. Authorities emphasize prioritizing Dudepo because of geographic isolation, while local clinics (puskesmas) coordinate with village authorities to monitor developments and maintain surveillance. Medical teams remain on site to ensure cases receive appropriate care and to support lifting the KLB as transmission is brought under control. Cross-sector cooperation is strengthened to ensure medicines and vitamin A for infected children, with plans to extend monitoring to surrounding areas if needed.

triage.headline_ja: ゴロンタロ州保健局、ドゥデポ島村での麻疹アウトブレイクに迅速対応
triage.triage_reason: 地域限定的な麻疹アウトブレイクで地元保健当局が既に対応中だが、感染規模や重症度の詳細が不明であり、遠隔地でのワクチン接種率低下によるさらなる拡大の可能性があるため経過観察が必要。
triage.notes: 地元保健局が既にKLB（アウトブレイク）宣言し、疫学調査・追加ワクチン接種・住民スクリーニングなどの対応を実施中。感染者数や重症度データが記事に記載されておらず、今後の拡大有無を注視する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: India delivers medical aid to Kenya to bolster Ebola preparedness
article.articleSummary: India delivered a 4.5-tonne shipment of essential medical supplies to Kenya to bolster Ebola preparedness and future pandemics, with 279 packages unloaded at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport in Nairobi. High Commissioner Dr Adarsh Swaika handed the items to Health Secretary Aden Duale. The consignment includes PPE kits, sample-transport containers, infrared thermometers, face shields and boots, to strengthen Kenya National Public Health Institute’s surveillance, safe sample collection and transport, and infection-prevention for frontline workers. A second tranche is expected soon. This follows more than 45 tonnes of similar supplies sent to Africa CDC in late May–early June 2026. The broader Kenya-India health cooperation includes 1.12 million COVID-19 vaccine doses under Vaccine Maitri and support such as a Bhabhatron radiotherapy machine, CT/MRI services. Over 10,000 Kenyans travel to India annually for treatment; Indian pharma accounts for over half of Kenya’s medicines market.

triage.triage_reason: 本記事はケニアにおけるエボラ発生の報告ではなく、インドからケニアへの防疫体制強化を目的とした医療物資支援に関する内容であり、実際の感染症発生・流行を示す情報はない。
triage.notes: 記事はケニアでのエボラ発生ではなく、備え・支援体制強化（preparedness）に関する二国間協力の報道。ケニアは対象国リストに含まれず、インドは支援提供国であり発生国ではないためverified_locationsは空とした。

article.articleHeadline: Pune: Dengue Cases Surge In July As Intermittent Rains Boost Mosquito Breeding
article.articleSummary: Dengue in Pune, India surges in July as intermittent rains boost Aedes breeding. For the first three weeks of July, Pune Municipal Corporation reports 540 suspected dengue cases and 22 lab-confirmed infections, up from 175 suspected and 12 confirmed in June. Warje-Karvenagar ward records the highest numbers, followed by Nagar Road-Wadgaonsheri, Kothrud, and Aundh-Baner. Health officials attribute the spike to stagnant water from intermittent rainfall that creates mosquito breeding sites. Patients show dengue-like symptoms; some require hospitalization for high fever, dehydration, low platelets, and severe pain. Early diagnosis, hydration, rest, and paracetamol are advised; antibiotics are ineffective and no antiviral exists. Children are affected, and confirmation remains essential. No major chikungunya outbreak this year. PMC urges residents to remove stagnant water, cover water storage, use repellents and nets, and seek testing for high fever, rash, or severe joint pain.

triage.headline_ja: プネー：断続的な降雨による蚊の繁殖増加で7月にデング熱症例が急増
triage.triage_reason: 季節性のデング熱増加であり、例年見られる蚊媒介感染症の流行パターンに近い。重症度や国際的拡大の兆候は乏しいが、雨季による蚊媒介環境の継続と流行しやすさから経過観察が妥当。

article.articleHeadline: 综述丨非洲埃博拉死亡病例过千 疫情尚未达峰
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Review | The African Ebola death toll has surpassed 1,000; the outbreak has not yet peaked.
article.articleSummary: Democratic Republic of the Congo (Ituri and North Kivu) and Uganda are experiencing an Ebola virus disease outbreak caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, with fatalities surpassing 1,000. As of July 20, DRC reported 2,473 confirmed cases and 999 deaths; Uganda had 20 cases and 2 deaths, making total deaths over 1,000. The outbreak is the third-largest on record and has accelerated over the past month. While some areas show stabilization, the epidemic has not peaked: over 80% of new infections are not linked to known contacts, and many deaths occur outside care facilities. Ituri hosts 16 internally displaced person camps with over 270,000 displaced, raising transmission risk. Congo has 23 treatment centers, 19 laboratories, and about 800 beds; 121 health workers infected, 36 dead. Uganda’s last patient recovered on July 16, with a 42-day observation period remaining. No approved vaccine or therapy; trials underway. Cross-border risks to South Sudan persist.

article.articleHeadline: Pemkot Pekalongan mempercepat deteksi dini TBC guna cegah penularan
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Pekalongan City Government Accelerates Early Detection of TB to Prevent Transmission.
article.articleSummary: Tuberculosis (TB) control in Pekalongan, Central Java, Indonesia, is shifting to proactive detection. The Pekalongan City Health Department reports 140 TB patients currently undergoing treatment. To curb transmission, the Active Case Finding (ACF) program will run from July 2026 through September 2026, targeting about 1,350 people for screening. Health workers, together with Mentari Sehat Indonesia cadres, will visit the homes and surrounding contacts of diagnosed patients to test close contacts. Symptoms to watch include a cough lasting more than two weeks, fever, especially at night, and loss of appetite. Transmission is influenced by factors such as poor environmental sanitation and contacts with untreated TB cases. Treatment typically lasts at least six months; in certain cases therapy can extend to one or two years depending on severity. All age groups are at risk, and early screening is encouraged for those with symptoms or close contact with TB patients.

triage.headline_ja: プカロンガン市政府、結核の感染拡大防止へ早期発見を加速
triage.triage_reason: 既存の結核対策プログラムに関する通常業務報告であり、異常な増加や新規変異等の特筆すべき事象は見られない。
triage.notes: 地域の結核対策における能動的症例探索(ACF)プログラムの実施報告であり、通常の公衆衛生活動の範囲内と判断される。

article.articleHeadline: 全国已有多地拉响蚊媒传染病警报 防控形势严峻
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Several regions nationwide have sounded mosquito-borne disease alerts, and the prevention and control situation is grave.
article.articleSummary: As of July 23, 2026, multiple regions across southern, eastern, and South China have issued mosquito-borne disease alerts, with the control situation described as grave. Prolonged heat and heavy rainfall since early summer have created extensive standing water, boosting Aedes albopictus (white-striped mosquito) breeding—the main vector for dengue fever, which presents with high fever, muscle pain, and rash; severe cases can involve organ bleeding. Culex mosquitoes near water bodies raise the risk of Japanese encephalitis, affecting elderly and children. Border regions face ongoing malaria importation risk, enabling local transmission upon bites. Sporadic imported cases have been reported, increasing community transmission risk. In response, authorities launched comprehensive anti-mosquito campaigns, including removal of standing water, fogging in old neighborhoods, markets, schools, and parks; door-to-door public education; fever clinics with rapid mosquito-borne disease testing; and enhanced entry screening at ports and other borders.

triage.headline_ja: 全国の複数地域で蚊媒介感染症警報発令、防疫情勢は厳しい状況
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準は該当なしだが、WPRO基準（長期曝露・流行しやすさ）が複数該当し、全国的な警報発令という社会的関心の高まりも確認されるため、フルRRAでの確認が望ましい。
triage.notes: 記事は季節性の蚊媒介感染症（デング熱、日本脳炎、マラリア）に関する全国的な予防警報であり、具体的な症例数・死亡者数の記載はない。長期の高温多雨による蚊の繁殖環境拡大と、国境地域での輸入マラリア例が言及されている。政府による大規模な防蚊対策が実施されており、季節性の予防的対応の色合いが強い。

article.articleHeadline: Počet potvrdených obetí eboly v Kongu narástol na vyše tisíc
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The number of confirmed Ebola deaths in Congo has risen to over a thousand.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease outbreaks in the Democratic Republic of the Congo have risen to more than 1,000 confirmed deaths and about 2,500 infections as of July 23, 2026, according to ČTK/Reuters. This marks the fastest-spreading Ebola outbreak in history. The article reports ongoing transmission within the DRC and highlights the unprecedented pace of spread relative to past outbreaks. No details are given on laboratory confirmation, infection sources, or specific containment measures. The figures underscore the scale and severity of the current epidemic in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, signaling a critical turn in the disease's trajectory for public health planning.

article.articleHeadline: राज्यात साथीच्या आजारांचा वाढला धोका
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The risk of infectious diseases has increased in the state.
article.articleSummary: As of 23 July 2026, renewed rainfall in Mumbai and Pune after a ten-day lull has heightened the risk of dengue, malaria, and chikungunya. In the first week of the month, heavy rain was followed by 8–10 days of dry spell, leaving water to stagnate in rooftop tanks, pots, old tires, coconut husks, metal drums, and other containers, creating breeding grounds for Aedes and Anopheles larvae. Public health authorities urge residents to cover water storage, clean containers weekly, and seek prompt medical testing and treatment for fever or suspicious symptoms. Hospitals have been notified; private facilities must register dengue and malaria cases on the state health department portal. The city is deploying biological larvicide sprays along drains, river-adjacent water bodies, and settlements, plus liquid biological formulations to curb larvae. Authorities stress sanitation and eliminating stagnant water to support official vector-control efforts.

triage.notes: マハラシュトラ州（ムンバイ・プネ）における季節的な媒介蚊由来感染症（デング熱、マラリア、チクングニア）のリスク増加に関する予防的注意喚起記事。地方自治体による通常の対策（幼虫駆除、報告義務化等）が既に実施されており、突発的なアウトブレイクの兆候は記載なし。

article.articleHeadline: 非洲埃博拉死亡病例过千，疫情尚未达峰
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Africa's Ebola death toll surpasses 1,000 as the outbreak has not yet peaked.
article.articleSummary: Ebola death toll in Africa's current outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and Uganda exceeds 1,000 deaths, with 999 in Congo and 2 in Uganda as of July 20, 2026. The DRC reports 2,473 confirmed cases; Uganda 20. The outbreak centers on Ituri Province (Bunia hub; Mongbwalu) with spillover risk to Goma in North Kivu. Congo has 23 treatment centers and 19 laboratories, about 800 beds in use (86.7% occupancy). At least 121 health workers have been infected, 36 of them dead. Ituri hosts at least 16 displacement camps with over 270,000 people, increasing transmission risk. The outbreak is caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus; no approved vaccines or therapies exist though candidates are in trials. WHO declared the outbreak a Public Health Emergency of International Concern; Uganda has entered a 42-day post-recovery observation after the last case, while cross-border movement remains a containment challenge.

article.articleHeadline: В ДР Конго число погибших о Эболы возросло до 1 033 человека
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: In DR Congo, the death toll from Ebola has risen to 1,033 people.
article.articleSummary: As of 23 July 2026, Ebola virus disease in DR Congo has 2,536 confirmed cases across five provinces, with 738 in isolation or hospital, 506 recoveries and 1,033 fatalities (case fatality rate 40.7%), and a contact-tracing rate of 77.2%. Ituri province remains the epicenter. Response efforts are expanding the capacity of response teams, laboratories and health facilities; contact tracing is intensified, entry-point controls are reinforced, and population information campaigns are underway. Additional material, technical and medical support is strengthening on-site measures to curb transmission and sustain outbreak control in the affected regions. The update is from the Ministry of Communications and Media. These figures reflect ongoing outbreak conditions and the capacity to curb further spread.

article.articleHeadline: ارتفاع الإصابات المؤكدة بفيروس إيبولا إلى 2536 في الكونغو
