article.articleHeadline: Congo's Ebola deaths top 1,000 as violence and shortages hamper medics | CNBC Africa
article.articleSummary: Democratic Republic of Congo reports 1,033 Ebola deaths among 2,536 confirmed cases as of July 23, 2026, in the Bundibugyo strain outbreak (17th DRC Ebola outbreak) declared mid-May. No approved vaccine for Bundibugyo, which carries up to 40% fatality; experimental vaccines and treatments are under review, with limited data on effectiveness. The outbreak is intensified by insecurity in eastern Congo, shortages of basic supplies, and attacks on clinics, hindering response. The virus has spread to neighboring Uganda, which has 20 confirmed cases; no new Ugandan cases since June 22 and the last patient was discharged on July 16, triggering a 42-day countdown to virus-free status. Transmission occurs via direct contact with bodily fluids; symptoms include fever, vomiting, diarrhea, and bleeding. Community distrust and burial restrictions compound outbreak challenges.

article.articleHeadline: Cómo la minería ilegal de oro ha provocado un repunte de la malaria en la Amazonía
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: How illegal gold mining has sparked a malaria resurgence in the Amazon.
article.articleSummary: Illegal gold mining in Brazil's Amazon Yanomami territory is linked to a malaria resurgence, with researchers from Stanford, Federal University of Mato Grosso, and Federal University of Minas Gerais quantifying the impact using Brazilian Health Ministry data. By January 2023, about 20,000 illegal miners operated in the Yanomami lands, roughly two-thirds of the indigenous population. Malaria testing showed near-universal positivity among those tested. The study finds that each 0.03% increase in mining activity correlates with a 20-46% rise in malaria cases one to two years later, amounting to roughly a 300% increase in malaria within the Yanomami territory from 2016 to 2023. Mechanisms include deforestation and riverbank breaches creating mosquito breeding grounds, introduction of parasites by miners moving from high-incidence areas, and mercury use contaminating water and weakening immunity. Lula's government began steps to expel illegal miners, as Bolsonaro's deregulation preceded the crisis.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: India Has Sent 4.5 Tons of Medical Aid to Kenya to Strengthen Its Preparedness to Deal with Ebola
article.articleSummary: India sent 4.5 metric tons of medical aid to Kenya to bolster preparedness against Ebola and other infectious diseases. The first batch was handed over at Nairobi's Jomo Kenyatta International Airport to Kenya's Health Minister Aden Duale. This follows India’s earlier shipments totaling over 45 tons to Africa CDC in May and June to strengthen the continent's Ebola readiness. Kenya has been among the first to receive Indian assistance during public health emergencies; during the COVID-19 pandemic, the Vaccine Maitri program supplied Kenya with 1.12 million vaccine doses, along with medicines and other medical support. The initiative underscores ongoing bilateral cooperation to enhance surveillance, rapid response, and clinical capacity for infectious disease threats in Africa.

article.articleHeadline: 'I need some rest': CJP leader Abhijeet Dipke leaves Jantar Mantar protest after falling ill; suffers fever, food poisoning suspected

As of 23 July 2026, he reported a high fever and severe body pains, later posting on X that he needed rest and would return by evening. CJP spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka said vomiting and diarrhoea suggest possible food poisoning, with concerns about contaminated food, including a fear of deliberate tampering. Dipke also experienced vomiting and dizziness earlier in the week. The protest movement remains deadlocked with the government; Nadda invited talks at his office, which the protesters declined, demanding neutral-location discussions.

article.articleHeadline: India Sends Medical Aid To Kenya To Boost Ebola Readiness
article.articleSummary: India sent 4.5 tonnes of medical aid to Kenya to boost Ebola readiness, handed over at Nairobi's Jomo Kenyatta International Airport by Indian High Commissioner Adarsh Swaika to Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale. The 279-package consignment includes PPE kits, sample transport kits, infrared thermometers, face shields and heavy-duty boots, and aims to strengthen Kenya's disease surveillance, safe sample collection/transport, infection prevention, and frontline worker protection against Ebola and other infectious diseases. This follows India’s delivery of over 45 tonnes of aid to the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention for Ebola preparedness, and earlier Vaccine Maitri shipments delivering 1.12 million COVID-19 doses to Kenya. A second tranche will be delivered soon. The partnership also covers grants for medical equipment, including a Bhabhatron radiotherapy machine for Kenyatta National Hospital and diagnostic gear for the Kenya Navy Hospital in Mombasa. More than 10,000 Kenyans travel to India each year for medical treatment.

article.articleHeadline: فيروس إيبولا يقتل 1033 أشخاص في الكونغو الديمقراطية
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola virus kills 1,033 people in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has reached 2,536 confirmed cases and 1,033 deaths, with 63 new infections in the eastern provinces of Ituri, North Kivu and Haut-Uele. Neighboring Uganda, which had earlier reported no active cases, now shows two deaths and 20 new infections per WHO. The outbreak remains one of Africa’s deadliest, with Ebola having caused over 15,000 deaths in the region in five decades. The World Health Organization has initiated clinical trials on two new therapeutics for a rare Ebola strain and granted emergency use authorization for a molecular diagnostic test. Last week, a first trial assessed the safety of the ChAdOx1 vaccine led by Oxford University. WHO Ebola response lead Tierno Baldeh cautioned that the outbreak still outpaces containment efforts.

article.articleHeadline: 黑龙江发布夏季疾控提醒 重点防范四类高发传染病
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Heilongjiang Issues Summer Disease-Control Reminders, Emphasizing Four Categories of High-Incidence Infectious Diseases.
article.articleSummary: Harbin, Heilongjiang Province, China—A July 23 briefing by the provincial CDC outlines four categories of high-incidence summer infectious diseases. In the first 28 weeks of 2026, Class B infectious-disease reports fell 7.79% year-on-year, with no large-scale outbreaks and overall control stable, though humid heat raises risks for enteric, vector-borne, and zoonotic diseases. Enteric infections are the priority: Norovirus and infectious diarrhea spread via contaminated food, flood-season water contamination raises outbreak risk, and Hand-foot-and-mouth disease mainly affects children under five, with vesicles and fever (rarely encephalitis). In forested areas, ticks pose forest encephalitis risk; Brucellosis outbreaks threaten livestock-slaughter workers and consumers of raw beef/lamb, causing recurrent fever and joint pain. Respiratory diseases remain low, with sporadic influenza and COVID-19, but human metapneumovirus and rhinovirus circulate, underscoring protection in enclosed spaces. Preventive guidance emphasizes food safety, outdoor protection, prompt care with exposure history, and prudent heat-avoidance measures.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola en RDC : le bilan dépasse les 1.000 morts
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in the DR Congo: death toll surpasses 1,000.
article.articleSummary: Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo continues, with 1,033 deaths and 2,536 confirmed cases reported as of July 21, per the latest situation update. A total of 506 people have recovered, and 738 remain in isolation. No new health zones were added, keeping 47 zones affected across five provinces. The outbreak remains in a sustained transmission phase with high virus circulation. In North Kivu, 182 patients are in isolation for a capacity of 141 beds (occupancy 129.1%). At a Bunia briefing, Adélard Lufongola, head of the Ebola response, noted a plateau in case notifications in some areas, but it is too early to say the outbreak has peaked. The virus strain is Bundibugyo; ongoing transmission is fueled by population movement, insecurity, artisanal mining, and cross-border exchanges with Uganda and South Sudan.

article.articleHeadline: 민주콩고, 두 달만에 1천 명 사망...에볼라 확산세 역대 최고
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Democratic Republic of the Congo, 1,000 deaths in just two months... Ebola spread at an all-time high.
article.articleSummary: Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has surged to 2,473 confirmed cases and 1,031 deaths (case fatality rate 41.6%) as of July 22, 2026, marking the deadliest and fastest-spreading outbreak in the country. First cases emerged on May 15, and the two-month toll now outpaces the 2013–2016 outbreak’s pace. About 80% of new patients have no known transmission link, hindering containment. Response efforts are disrupted by wage arrears triggering strikes among healthcare workers and response personnel—including funeral teams, epidemiologists, drivers, and community surveillance—complicating operations. The WHO warns funding shortages exacerbate the crisis, with reduced U.S. aid and limited international support. If not contained, experts warn the outbreak could spill over and resemble a West Africa-wide epidemic, underscoring urgent public health measures and sustained funding.

article.articleHeadline: What experts are saying as Ebola outbreak in Congo and Uganda kills more that 1,000 people
article.articleSummary: Eastern Congo's Ebola outbreak—the fastest-growing in history—has 2,536 confirmed cases and 1,033 deaths, with at least 738 people in isolation or hospitalized as of July 23, 2026. The Bundibugyo virus driving the outbreak has no approved vaccine or treatment. About 90% of cases are in Ituri province; additional cases have emerged in Kisangani and in neighboring Uganda, which reports 20 cases and 2 deaths, all imported from Congo. A June case in France involved a doctor traveling from Congo who recovered. Global risk is low, but WHO assigns very high risk inside Congo and high risk in Uganda due to cross-border spread. Transmission remains sustained; reporting delays and data consolidation slow understanding of spread. Contact tracing monitors about 77% of known contacts (vs. 95% target). No vaccine or treatment exists, and imported cases are probable but currently contained.

article.articleHeadline: Son's dengue claim wrongly rejected, insurer ordered to pay father Rs 1.11 lakh
article.articleSummary: Punjab: District Consumer Commission, Ropar, ordered Future Health Suraksha Family Floater to reimburse Rs 90,079 for a son’s dengue treatment (Oct 1–9, 2021 at Kaushal Multi-Speciality Hospital, Kharar) plus 9% interest from Jan 24, 2022, Rs 10,000 for mental agony, and Rs 11,000 in litigation costs. Premium Rs 19,404 for the policy period 30 Jun 2021–29 Jun 2022. The insurer had repudiated the claim citing medical-record discrepancies (treatment timings, Google Timeline data, missing lab clarifications). The commission held that minor discrepancies cannot establish fraud, noting patients cannot control hospital records and the burden to prove fraud lies with the insurer, which failed to present credible evidence. The broker was not held liable. The ruling reinforces fair processing of genuine health-insurance claims and protection against arbitrary repudiation by insurers.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: This is the hometown of five women involved in online prostitution in Ende; one is pregnant and the others have syphilis.
article.articleSummary: Ende Regency, Flores, Indonesia — Five young women from Flores were detained in Ende for alleged online prostitution; the women are from Ngada (SO, BKS, VNG), Lembata (KPU), and Manggarai (CAJN), ages 16–19, with one pregnant. The operation is thought to be coordinated by a pimp named Umi, who connects the workers with clients at 200,000–300,000 IDR per encounter; Umi takes 50,000 IDR per transaction, while the kos house owner NJA receives 2,250,000 IDR per lease, with a daily earnings target of 1,000,000 IDR. Health screening at Puskesmas Onekore showed one syphilis diagnosis, three with reactive syphilis serology needing further testing, and one pregnancy. The case remains under investigation, with NJA and Umi summoned but not attending. Notably, the individuals were not Ende locals, underscoring sexually transmitted infection concerns linked to cross-regional networks in Flores and Ende.

article.articleHeadline: Više od tisuću osoba umrlo od ebole u DR Kongo
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: More than a thousand people have died of Ebola in the DR Congo.
article.articleSummary: As of July 23, 2026, Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo has surpassed 1,000 deaths with 2,536 confirmed cases, according to the DR Congo Public Health Institute. This marks the 17th Ebola outbreak in the country, officially declared in mid-May, though experts believe transmission began several weeks earlier. The outbreak is caused by the rare Bundibugyo strain, which can have a case-fatality rate up to 40%, and there is no approved vaccine or specific therapeutics for this strain. Health authorities confront insecurity in eastern Congo, the outbreak epicenter, where dozens of armed groups operate; in addition to shortages of basic medical supplies, there have been attacks on health facilities by local populations.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国でエボラ出血熱により1000人以上が死亡
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱の大規模アウトブレイク（死者1000人超、症例2536件）で致死率の高い稀な株が原因、かつ治安不安による対応困難が重なり、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するため。
triage.notes: Bundibugyo株による第17次アウトブレイク。ワクチン・治療薬未承認、東部の武力紛争・医療施設への攻撃により対応が著しく困難な状況。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola death toll in DR Congo surpasses 1,000
article.articleSummary: Ebola in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo has killed over 1,000 people. As of July 23, 2026, officials report 2,536 cases and 1,033 deaths since the May 15 outbreak began, with Ituri province as the epicenter. The disease has spread to Tshopo and Haut-Uele, including Kisangani in Tshopo, where four deaths have been recorded. The pace is the fastest on record: 2,000 confirmed cases were reached in two months, versus 10 months in the 2018–2019 outbreak. The response faces severe constraints: fragile hospitals, lagging contact tracing, and a funding gap in the WHO/Africa CDC plan of about $400+ million of a $518 million target. Prime Minister Judith Suminwa plans to visit hotspots with US and UN officials to assess ground realities. Ituri’s displacement camps (over 900,000 people) and mobile artisanal mining workers amplify transmission; health workers report pay shortages and centers operating at full capacity, delaying care.

triage.headline_ja: DRコンゴのエボラ死者数が1,000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱がDRコンゴで急速に拡大し2,536症例・1,033死亡と過去最速のペースで増加、複数州へ拡大し資金不足・医療体制の逼迫が深刻なためIHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当。
triage.notes: 2018-2019年の流行と比較し過去最速の拡大ペース。避難民キャンプ（90万人超）や移動性の高い鉱山労働者が感染拡大を助長。WHO/Africa CDCの対応計画に約1億ドル超の資金不足あり。国際支援（米国・国連関係者の視察予定）が示唆されている。

article.articleHeadline: Minas de oro, las incubadoras del ébola
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Gold mines, the incubators of Ebola.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak centered in Mongbwalu, Ituri Province, Democratic Republic of the Congo, with more than 1,300 infections and 754 confirmed deaths and rising. Transmission is not airborne; infection occurs via direct contact with infected fluids (blood, vomit, saliva, sweat, feces, breast milk, semen) through broken skin or mucous membranes. Conditions around Mongbwalu—hundreds of thousands of residents in gold-mining camps—create a perfect amplifier: crowded underground pits, shared water and tools, and trucks moving ore to multiple provinces. Mercury is used to amalgamate gold; miners and families face chronic exposure to toxic mercury in a setting of dangerous living/working conditions. The article links the outbreak to the region’s mining economy and social dynamics, including low wages around $24/week for laborers and gendered roles with women mostly on the surface.

triage.headline_ja: 金鉱、エボラの培養器
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国イトゥリ州で1,300人以上感染・754人死亡とされるエボラ出血熱の大規模アウトブレイクであり、IHR基準の複数該当及び国際的関心が高い事案。
triage.notes: 鉱山労働者コミュニティにおける密集した生活環境と複数州への鉱石輸送が感染拡大リスクを高めている。致死率が高く(754/1300超)、continuing outbreakとして厳重な監視が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Epidemija uzima maha: Opaki virus usmrtio više od 1000 ljudi! Nema cjepiva ni lijeka
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The epidemic is taking hold: A deadly virus has killed more than 1,000 people! There is no vaccine or cure.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (eastern region) persists. As of July 23, 2026, deaths exceed 1,000 and confirmed cases reach 2,536, per the Public Health Institute; 63 new cases and 34 deaths have been reported since the last update. This marks the 17th Ebola outbreak in the DRC, officially declared mid-May but likely spreading weeks earlier. The culprit is Bundibugyo ebolavirus, with case fatality up to 40%; there is no approved vaccine or specific treatment for this strain. Security instability with armed groups in the eastern epicenter and attacks on health facilities impede response. Transmission occurs via direct contact with bodily fluids of infected living or deceased individuals; symptoms include fever, vomiting, diarrhea, and bleeding in severe cases. The outbreak has reached Uganda, which reports 20 confirmed cases, with no new cases since June 22 and a 42-day countdown after the last patient's discharge on July 16.

triage.headline_ja: エピデミックが拡大：凶悪なウイルスが1000人以上を死亡させた！ワクチンも治療薬もない
triage.triage_reason: DRC東部で第17次エボラ流行が継続し死者1000人超・感染2536人に達し、ウガンダへの越境拡大も確認されているため、複数のIHR基準に該当しフルRRAが必要。
triage.notes: ウガンダへの拡大が報告されているが、ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めていない。武装勢力による治安不安が対応の障害となっており、承認済みワクチン・治療薬が存在しないBundibugyo株である点も重大リスク。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola pochłonęła już ponad tysiąc ofiar. Dezinformacja utrudnia walkę
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola has already claimed more than a thousand victims. Disinformation is hindering the fight.
article.articleSummary: In the Democratic Republic of Congo's Ituri province, Ebola deaths reach 999 with Uganda reporting 2 more deaths and 20 infections; total fatalities exceed 1,000 and confirmed cases surpass 2,400. Declared on May 15, this outbreak is the fastest-growing Ebola epidemic in history, with about 80% of new infections not linked to known transmission chains and the virus spreading beyond Ituri to other regions. Disinformation fuels fear, with misinformation that health workers kill patients, attacks on clinics and staff number at least 12, and some health workers dying after infection, amid pay arrears. The current wave is driven by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, for which no approved vaccine or treatment exists. Oxford University researchers began trials of an experimental vaccine targeting this strain, and two new drugs are being tested in Ituri. WHO is expanding rapid-response teams and epidemiologic surveillance.

triage.headline_ja: エボラの犠牲者はすでに1000人を超えた。偽情報が対策を困難にしている
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱がDRC・ウガンダで拡大し死者1000人超、80%が感染経路不明で承認されたワクチン・治療薬が存在しないため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する重大シグナル。
triage.notes: ウガンダでの死亡・感染例も報告されているが、ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めていない。Bundibugyo型エボラウイルスによる史上最速の流行拡大で、偽情報による医療従事者への攻撃も発生している点が特筆される。

article.articleHeadline: Why health officials do not have a good handle on the current Ebola outbreak
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo: after just over two months, nearly 1,000 deaths and more than 2,400 infections, with daily case counts not slowing. The outbreak currently lacks an approved vaccine. About 80% of new cases occur outside known contacts, underscoring gaps in contact tracing. The affected region features transient workers and ongoing conflict, complicating case follow-up. WHO is training about 21,000 community workers to improve tracing capacity. Roughly two-thirds of deaths occur outside the health system as many symptom-presenters seek traditional healers or hesitate to enter clinics, amid stigma and mistrust toward responders. Experts say building trust and expanding access to care are critical. Promising but limited progress includes clinical trials for treatments and a post-exposure drug, available only through trials, that could prevent illness after exposure.

triage.headline_ja: 現行のエボラ出血熱アウトブレイクを保健当局が十分に把握できていない理由
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準に複数該当（重大な公衆衛生影響、異常性、国際拡大リスク）し、WPRO基準も全て該当するため、フルリスク評価に進むべきシグナルと判断。
triage.notes: 発症から2ヶ月余りで死者約1000人、感染者2400人超と急速に拡大中。承認済みワクチンがなく、新規症例の8割が既知の接触者外で発生、紛争地域での移動労働者も多く、接触者追跡が困難。WHOは約2.1万人のコミュニティワーカーを訓練中だが、死亡の3分の2は医療システム外で発生しており、対応者への不信・スティグマが課題。

article.articleHeadline: RDC : Save the Children alerte sur 189 enfants morts d'Ebola en Ituri
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: DRC: Save the Children warns that 189 children have died of Ebola in Ituri.
article.articleSummary: As of July 23, 2026, Ebola remains active in the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, centered in Ituri province. Save the Children reports 189 child deaths among 476 lab-confirmed pediatric infections since the outbreak was officially declared on May 15, 2026, with the child deaths accounting for over 20% of all confirmed virus fatalities. In Ituri, the organization is supporting over 4,000 children with mental health and psychosocial services, operating more than 18 child-friendly spaces (fixed and mobile) offering reading, drawing, singing, games, clay modeling, and relaxation to address trauma. Teams note fear of transmission is reshaping behavior, with many children avoiding physical contact and some separated from parents or guardians due to illness, death, isolation, or displacement, sometimes requiring temporary care. With September school resumption approaching and new cases continuing, Save the Children calls for increased international funding for child protection, mental health, and psychosocial support in eastern DRC.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国：セーブ・ザ・チルドレン、イトゥリ州でエボラにより189人の子どもが死亡と警鐘
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱の継続的アウトブレイクにより多数の小児死亡が報告されており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 2026年5月15日に公式宣言されたエボラアウトブレイクが継続中。小児感染476例中189例が死亡し、全体死亡者の20%以上を占める。国際支援（資金）を明示的に要請しており社会的関心も高い。国境を越えた拡大リスクや渡航制限については記事内で言及なし。

article.articleHeadline: Mortes por Ebola no Congo ultrapassam 1.000 enquanto a violência e escassez de suprimentos prejudicam médicos
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Deaths from Ebola in the Congo surpass 1,000 as violence and shortages of supplies hinder doctors.
article.articleSummary: Death toll from Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo exceeds 1,000, with 2,536 confirmed cases and 1,033 deaths (as of the latest report). The 17th Congo outbreak, declared in mid-May, is caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, which has up to 40% fatality and currently lacks an approved vaccine. Health workers face insecurity from armed groups, attacks on clinics, and chronic shortages of supplies, complicating containment. Transmission occurs via direct contact with bodily fluids; symptoms include fever, vomiting, diarrhea, and in severe cases bleeding. A small number of experimental vaccines and treatments are under evaluation, with limited animal data supporting cross-use. The outbreak has spilled over into Uganda, which reports 20 confirmed cases; no new Ugandan cases since 22 June, and the last patient was discharged on 16 July, with a 42-day countdown to declare elimination. Since the last report, Congo added 63 cases and 34 deaths.

article.articleHeadline: Minas de oro, las incubadoras del ébola | El Diario Montañés
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Gold Mines, the Ebola Incubators | El Diario Montañés
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in Mongbwalu, Ituri Province, northeast Democratic Republic of the Congo, linked to gold mining. The outbreak has surpassed 1,300 infections with 754 confirmed deaths; not the largest on record—the 2014–2016 West Africa outbreak killed about 11,300 and sickened over 28,000—but it began with the worst first month of cases ever recorded. Transmission requires direct contact with infected fluids—blood, vomit, sweat, feces, saliva, breast milk, or semen—through broken skin or mucous membranes; it is not airborne. The mines surrounding Mongbwalu, housing about 130,000 residents, create ideal amplification: crowded tunnels, flooded pits, poor ventilation, shared water, and cross-contamination as trucks haul ore. Wages are meager; miners work under harsh conditions, often under ground for days to weeks. Mercury is used to extract gold, producing toxic vapors when amalgams are heated; mercury exposure predated the Ebola alert. The mine environment accelerates spread across provinces via ore-driven transport.

triage.headline_ja: 金鉱山、エボラのインキュベーター | El Diario Montañés
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国イトゥリ州で1,300人以上の感染、754人の死亡が報告されるエボラ出血熱の大規模アウトブレイクであり、鉱山労働環境による地域間拡散のリスクが高いためフルRRAが必要。

article.articleHeadline: Над илјада починати од ебола во ДР Конго

article.articleHeadline: Covid-19: दक्षिण भारत के बाद बिहार में भी पहुंचा कोरोना, क्या फिर पूरे देश में फैल सकता है वायरस? डॉक्टरों ने बताया
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: COVID-19: After South India, the coronavirus has also reached Bihar; could the virus spread across the entire country again? Doctors explain.
article.articleSummary: COVID-19 cases are rising again across India, with Andhra Pradesh reporting four deaths in recent days as the virus expands to Kerala, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, and Maharashtra. Bihar’s Bhagalpur has recorded infections in a father and daughter who are admitted to ICU. Delhi’s Safdarjung Hospital and public health expert Dr. Chandrakant Lahariya state the virus remains in circulation globally and continues to evolve, with XFG (Stratus), NB.1.8.1 and Cicada (BA.3.2) driving many current infections. Symptoms mirror flu: fever, dry or productive cough, sore throat, body aches, and headache; distinguishable progression includes breathing difficulties. Most infections are mild; deaths occur mainly in people with pre-existing conditions such as heart disease, kidney disease, or cancer. Monsoon season amplifies respiratory illnesses, but widespread nationwide spread is unlikely. Booster doses are not currently deemed necessary in India; preventive measures advised: avoid crowds, avoid antibiotics without doctors, and limit exposure in infected areas.

triage.headline_ja: COVID-19：南インドに続きビハール州にもコロナが到達、再び全国に拡大する可能性は？医師が解説

article.articleHeadline: El brote de ébola en la República Democrática del Congo supera los 1.000 muertos

Five provinces are affected: Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uele, and Tshopo, with sustained transmission and 738 patients hospitalized or isolated; 506 have recovered. Uganda reported 20 cases (15 imported from DRC) and 2 deaths; the last patient was discharged about a week ago, and Uganda observes a 42-day period without new cases to declare end. The outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo Ebola virus strain, with a 30–50% fatality rate and no approved vaccine or specific treatment. article.articleHeadline: World Insights: Fastest-ever Ebola outbreak tests global health response
article.articleSummary: On 23 July 2026, the Democratic Republic of the Congo faces the fastest Ebola outbreak on record, driven by the Bundibugyo strain. In just over two months it has reached 2,473 confirmed cases and 999 deaths, with Uganda reporting two deaths for a total toll of 1,001. Ituri province is the epicenter, responsible for over 90% of cases and about 80% of deaths; health workers account for more than 100 infections, including at least 36 fatalities. The Bundibugyo strain has no approved vaccines or specific treatments; Ervebo and monoclonal antibodies are ineffective against it. Early symptoms resemble malaria, delaying diagnosis. About 80% of new cases are outside known contact lists, and 66% of deaths occur in communities rather than facilities. IOM is expanding surveillance at 110 Points of Entry and 43 screening points; Kisangani reports imported cases from Ituri, while Mongbwalu shows signs of stabilization.

triage.headline_ja: 世界インサイト：史上最速のエボラ流行が世界の保健対応を試す
triage.triage_reason: 史上最速とされるエボラ出血熱（ブンディブギョ株）の流行がコンゴ民主共和国で発生し、確認症例2,473例・死者1,001例（ウガンダへの越境含む）に達しており、有効なワクチン・治療法がなく、医療従事者感染や地域内死亡も多いためIHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する重大シグナル。
triage.notes: ウガンダでも死亡例が報告されているが対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めていない。ブンディブギョ株には既存のワクチン（Ervebo）やモノクローナル抗体が無効であり、マラリアと初期症状が類似するため診断遅延が発生している点が重大なリスク要因。

article.articleHeadline: डेंगू से बचाव को बड़ी तैयारी, PMCH समेत राज्य के अस्पतालों में जल्द उपलब्ध होगी नई वैक्सीन
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Major preparations for dengue prevention; a new vaccine will soon be available in PMCH and other state hospitals.
article.articleSummary: Patna, Bihar — Dengue prevention gets a major upgrade as a Japan-developed dengue vaccine awaits rollout in Bihar after WHO and Indian government approvals. Once guidelines are issued, PMCH and other state hospitals will begin vaccination campaigns for people aged 4–60, protecting against all four dengue serotypes (DEN-1 to DEN-4) and aiming to reduce dengue hemorrhagic fever and fatalities. Vaccination centers will be established in hospitals; eligible individuals receive 0.5 mL, with primary and booster doses per protocol following medical screening and counseling. With an expected rise in dengue after August 15, preparations intensify: PMCH dengue ward capacity increasing from 10 to 20 beds (5 with ventilators); IGIMS, AIIMS Patna, and NMCH will reserve 10 beds each for dengue patients. Dengue testing will be free in all government hospitals. Areas identified as dengue-sensitive include Bazaar Committee, Kankarbagh, Rajiv Nagar, Shastrinagar, Fulwari Sharif, Indrapuri, Mahendru, Alamganj, and Transport Nagar.

triage.headline_ja: デング熱予防に向けた大規模な準備、PMCHを含む州内病院で新ワクチンが近く利用可能に
triage.triage_reason: デング熱流行に備えた予防的な医療体制整備（ワクチン導入・病床増設）に関する記事であり、異常な感染拡大や緊急性を示す内容ではない。
triage.notes: 季節性デング熱の流行前の予防的対応（ワクチン導入、病床拡充）を報じた記事であり、突発的アウトブレイクの報告ではない。Japanは発生地域ではなくワクチン開発国として言及されているため除外。

article.articleHeadline: इबोला अलर्ट पर बिहार सतर्क, अस्पतालों से तैयारियों का ब्योरा तलब
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Bihar on Ebola alert, seeks details from hospitals about preparations.
article.articleSummary: On July 23, 2026, Bihar activated Ebola preparedness following a central alert. The state health department Mandated major public hospitals and all district civil surgeons/CMOs to submit detailed readiness reports to the Centre, covering PPE kits, body bags, infection-control provisions, and other resources. Reports must include dates of PPE donning/doffing training, number of staff trained, and last mock drill. Hospitals listed include AIIMS Patna, IGIMS, all government medical colleges and hospitals, Ayush College, New Gardiner Road Hospital, Lok Nayak Jai Prakash Narayan Hospital, Rajendra Nagar Eye Hospital, Bihta ESIC Hospital, Bihar Mental Health Institute Koilvar, and other major facilities. This aligns with a June 29 directive from the Ministry of Health & Family Welfare to review Ebola preparedness across states. Ebola spreads via blood, bodily fluids, or contaminated objects; not airborne, highlighting the critical role of PPE and infection-control measures during care.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ警戒でビハール州が厳戒態勢、病院に準備状況の報告を要求
triage.triage_reason: インド中央政府の指令に基づく予防的な準備態勢の強化であり、実際のエボラ症例発生の報告はないため、現時点でのシグナルとしての緊急性は低いが、今後の動向を注視する必要がある。
triage.notes: 記事は実際のエボラ症例発生を報告しておらず、中央政府（保健家族福祉省）の6月29日付指令に基づく州レベルの予防的準備確認（PPE、感染対策、訓練状況の報告要求）に関するもの。実際の感染事例情報がないため、フルRRAへの移行は現時点で不要だが、続報（実症例の有無）を注視すべき。

article.articleHeadline: तेज बुखार को न करें नजरअंदाज! डेंगू-मलेरिया से बचाव के लिए डॉक्टर की अहम सलाह
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Don't ignore a high fever! Doctor's crucial advice for preventing dengue and malaria.
article.articleSummary: In Agra, Uttar Pradesh, rising monsoon rains have heightened the risk of dengue and malaria, according to Dr. Ashish Mittal, senior physician at Agra District Hospital. The seasonal conditions increase standing water where mosquitoes breed. No case counts are provided in the report, but officials warn of intensified transmission during monsoon. Prevention centers on eliminating stagnant water: do not let water collect in coolers, flower pots, tires, empty vessels, or buckets; drain and dry coolers weekly; keep premises clean and dry. Mosquitoes breed rapidly in these sites, so household-level measures are crucial to curb transmission during monsoon in Agra and broader Uttar Pradesh.

triage.headline_ja: 高熱を軽視しないで！デング熱・マラリア予防のための医師の重要なアドバイス
triage.triage_reason: 季節性のモンスーンに伴うデング熱・マラリアの一般的な予防啓発記事であり、具体的な症例数や異常な流行状況の報告はなく、通常の季節的注意喚起の範囲内である。
triage.notes: モンスーン時期の恒例的な予防啓発記事であり、症例数や異常な増加についての具体的データはない。継続的なモニタリングは不要と判断。

article.articleHeadline: Odisha Reports 2 New COVID-19 Cases, Total Infections Rise To 3
article.articleSummary: COVID-19 in Odisha rises to 3 cases with two new positives in Ganjam district, bringing the total to three. All three cases are in Ganjam; two new patients are under home isolation with stable condition; the third, a woman treated at MKCG Medical College and Hospital in Brahmapur, also stable. No serious symptoms or complications reported; officials say the overall COVID-19 situation is not serious and there is no immediate cause for concern. State health authorities note COVID-19 has become a common influenza-like disease and the virus has weakened. Independent assessments by IDSP and ICMR found no alarming trend. Routine surveillance continues. In response, hospitals in Ganjam have been directed to ensure mandatory COVID-19 testing for severe acute respiratory illness (SARI) and to conduct random testing of at least 5% of patients with influenza-like illness (ILI).

triage.headline_ja: オディシャ州でCOVID-19新規感染者2人、累計感染者数3人に
triage.triage_reason: 感染者数は3人と極めて少なく、症状も軽症で当局も懸念なしと発表しており、通常のサーベイランス範囲内の事象と判断される。
triage.notes: 当局はCOVID-19をインフルエンザ様疾患として扱い、深刻な事態ではないと明言。SARI/ILI患者への検査強化は通常のサーベイランス対応であり特筆すべき異常事態ではない。

article.articleHeadline: DR Congo's Ebola death toll hits 1033, confirmed cases exceed 2,500
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) remains in sustained transmission, caused by Bundibugyo virus, with Bunia in Ituri Province as the epicenter. As of July 23, 2026, deaths reached 1,033 and confirmed cases 2,536; 506 patients have recovered while 738 remain in isolation. Nationwide, 47 health zones across five provinces are affected, with 46 still under active transmission. North Kivu reports ongoing pressure on treatment capacity (182 in isolation vs 141 beds). No new affected health zone was reported. The outbreak’s persistence is driven by population movements, insecurity, artisanal mining, and cross-border exchanges with Uganda and South Sudan. Notifications show a plateau in some areas, but epidemiologically it is too early to declare a peak, and data delays may influence recent fluctuations. Public health response continues against sustained, high virus circulation.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ出血熱、死者1033人に、確定症例は2,500人を超える
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で持続的なエボラ出血熱の伝播が続き、死者1,033人・確定症例2,536人に達し、47保健区で活動的な感染が継続、治療キャパシティも逼迫しており、越境拡大リスクも指摘されているためフルRRAへ進めるべき。
triage.notes: ウガンダ・南スーダンとの越境リスクが指摘されているが、両国での確定症例発生は記事中で明示されておらず、対象国リストにも含まれないためverified_locationsからは除外した。

article.articleHeadline: فيروس إيبولا يفتك بـ 1033 شخصاً في الكونغو الديمقراطية
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola virus kills 1,033 people in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
article.articleSummary: On July 23, 2026, the Democratic Republic of the Congo reported 2,536 confirmed Ebola cases and 1,033 deaths, with dozens of new infections in the eastern region. The Congo’s Public Health Institute logged 63 new cases in Ituri and North Kivu, lifting the outbreak totals. Uganda had previously declared no active cases, but health authorities later confirmed two deaths and 20 new infections. Over five decades, Ebola has caused over 15,000 deaths in Africa, underscoring its severity. The World Health Organization announced clinical trials for two new therapeutics targeting the rare Ebola strain, granted emergency-use authorization for a new molecular diagnostic test, and launched a trial to assess the safety of the ChAdOx1 vaccine with Oxford University. A WHO official warned the outbreak continues to outpace response efforts.

triage.headline_ja: エボラウイルス、コンゴ民主共和国で1,033人の死者
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱による大規模な死者数（1,033人）と国境を越えたウガンダへの拡大が確認されており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するためフルRRAへの移行が必要。
triage.notes: ウガンダでの死亡例・感染例も報告されているが、対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めていない。WHOが治療薬治験・診断薬の緊急使用許可・ワクチン治験を実施するなど国際的対応が進行中。

locations.name: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

article.articleHeadline: El brote de ébola deja más de 1.000 muertos en RD Congo
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola outbreak leaves more than 1,000 dead in DR Congo.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (Ituri epicenter) has killed more than 1,000 people, with 1,031 confirmed deaths and 2,473 cases reported by the DRC Ministry of Health as of the latest update; about 737 patients are in isolation or receiving treatment. Declared on May 15, the outbreak is the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak on record and is caused by the Bundibugyo virus, for which no vaccines or treatments are approved. An experimental vaccine targeting Bundibugyo has begun the world’s first human trial (Phase I) in Oxford, testing safety and immune response in 50 healthy adults aged 18–55. Authorities warn that roughly 80% of new cases occur outside known transmission chains, with cases expanding to four additional provinces alongside Ituri. Experts warn the crisis could worsen, while CDC models suggest the worst case could approach the magnitude of Africa’s 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ流行、死者1,000人超に
triage.triage_reason: DRCでエボラ(ブンディブギョウイルス)による急速拡大の流行が発生し、致死率も高く、感染経路不明の症例が8割に上るなど国際的拡大リスクが高い。IHR4基準中複数該当。
triage.notes: 英国オックスフォードは治験実施地であり発生地ではないため除外。承認されたワクチン・治療薬がなく、CDCモデルでは2014-2016年西アフリカ流行に匹敵する可能性が指摘されている点は重大なリスク要因。

article.articleHeadline: Irish govt concerned as at least 930 people have died in DR Congo Ebola outbreak
article.articleSummary: At least 930 people have died in DR Congo's Ebola outbreak, with 2,344 confirmed cases as of Saturday night. Thirty-seven new deaths were recorded in the prior 24 hours, the fastest growth since the outbreak began on 15 May. The Bundibugyo virus drives this outbreak, with no approved vaccine or treatment. Ebola spreads from wildlife to humans and between people via bodily fluids and contaminated surfaces. The eastern region has five affected provinces, including Ituri, where rebel violence is restricting response. Authorities report at least 12 attacks on health facilities; 36 health workers infected and dead. The WHO warns that 80% of new cases arise from unknown transmission chains. DR Congo's health ministry says 724 patients are in isolation and in hospitals, with 22 recoveries in 24 hours, and response efforts intensified.

triage.headline_ja: アイルランド政府、DRコンゴのエボラ流行で少なくとも930人死亡に懸念表明
triage.triage_reason: DRコンゴでエボラ（ブンディブギョ株）による死者930人・確定症例2344人に達し、感染拡大速度が過去最速。武力紛争により対応が妨げられ、感染経路不明の症例が80%に上るなど国際的関心・支援の必要性が高い。
triage.notes: アイルランド政府による懸念表明が報じられているが、発生国はDRコンゴのみであり、アイルランドは対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsには含めない。WHOが感染経路不明の症例割合（80%）を警告しており、拡大リスクが高い。

article.articleHeadline: BRICS Health Ministers back TB research, disease surveillance, mental health cooperation
article.articleSummary: On 23 July 2026, BRICS Health Ministers in New Delhi and Chandigarh, India, concluded the 16th BRICS Health Ministers' Meeting under India's 2026 chairmanship, adopting a joint declaration to expand cooperation on tuberculosis (TB) research, disease surveillance, digital health, mental health, and access to medicines. Key outcomes include a stronger BRICS TB Research Network and a regional early warning mechanism for infectious diseases, plus closer collaboration among drug regulators and a BRICS Network of Centres of Excellence on Mental Wellness led by NIMHANS, India. A Sub-Working Group endorsed an Integrated Early Warning System for mass infectious diseases to improve surveillance, information sharing and coordinated responses. The declaration also establishes a BRICS Training Hub Network for mental health, strengthens regulatory alignment for medical products, and creates a BRICS Network of National Public Health Institutes. Digital health interoperability and ongoing vaccine, nuclear medicine and traditional medicine collaboration were endorsed.

triage.headline_ja: BRICS保健大臣会合、結核研究・疾病サーベイランス・メンタルヘルス協力を支持
triage.triage_reason: 本記事はBRICS保健大臣会合の政策的合意事項に関する報道であり、具体的な感染症の発生や公衆衛生上の緊急事態を報告するものではない。
triage.notes: 疾患名にTuberculosisが付与されているが、記事は具体的なTB発生事例ではなくBRICS諸国間の保健協力枠組みに関する会議報告。感染症イベントとしてのトリアージ対象外。

article.articleHeadline: Sud-Kivu : le Mpox toujours actif avec plus de 3 900 cas notifiés depuis début 2026
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: South Kivu: Mpox remains active with more than 3,900 cases reported since the beginning of 2026.
article.articleSummary: Mpox (monkeypox) remains active in South Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo, with 3,945 confirmed cases since the start of 2026 and a low case-fatality rate. Transmission spans 27 of 34 health zones, with Nyangezi health zone accounting for over 1,000 cases. Three deaths have been recorded this year. Some response partners have ceased operations, while the Provincial Health Division reports ongoing interventions to combat mpox. Although mpox has been declared no longer a current public health emergency in the DRC, surveillance and response continue in the province. The article also notes an Ebola outbreak in the DRC with 3 confirmed cases.

triage.headline_ja: 南キブ州：2026年初頭以降、Mpoxの発生が継続、確認症例3,900件超
triage.triage_reason: DRC南キブ州で2026年以降3,945件のMpox症例が継続し34保健地区中27地区に拡大、さらに新たなエボラ出血熱（確認3例）の発生も報告されており、公衆衛生上の懸念と国際的関心の観点からフルリスク評価が必要と判断される。
triage.notes: 記事はMpoxの継続的流行に加え、DRC国内での新たなエボラ出血熱（確認3例）の発生にも言及しており、複合的な公衆衛生上のリスクとして注視が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Mehr als 1000 Ebola-Tote
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: More than 1,000 Ebola deaths.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has caused 1,033 deaths and 2,536 infections, according to the national health institute, as of 23 July 2026. The outbreak remains ongoing, with sustained transmission and rising mortality. The article notes a continued public health response by authorities, but provides no details on specific affected provinces, laboratory confirmation processes, or the infection source. There is no information in the excerpt about imported or exported cases. The figures indicate a high burden and persistent spread, underscoring the need for ongoing surveillance and control measures in the DRC.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱による死者1,000人超
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱によるDRCでの死者1,000人超・感染者2,536人という大規模かつ継続的な流行であり、公衆衛生への深刻な影響と国際拡大リスクが認められるためフルRRAへ進める。
triage.notes: 感染源、具体的な発生州、輸入・輸出症例の有無、検査確定プロセスについて情報不足のため、続報での確認が必要。

article.articleHeadline: São Carlos registra queda de 98% nos casos de dengue
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: São Carlos records a 98% drop in dengue cases.
article.articleSummary: São Carlos, Brazil, reports a 98% reduction in dengue cases in 2026 (data up to July 23, 2026). The city has 396 confirmed dengue cases for 2026 to date, down from 19,312 in 2025. No dengue deaths have been recorded in 2026 so far. Total notifications—covering positive, awaiting results, and discarded cases—reach 3,116 in 2026, versus 25,312 in 2025 (an 88% drop). The surveillance bulletin also indicates that 171 chikungunya cases, 154 Zika virus cases, and 1 yellow fever case were discarded. Health authorities stress the importance of maintaining measures to prevent Aedes aegypti proliferation, notably eliminating breeding sites in residences and outdoor areas. The report underscores continued vigilance despite the favorable trend.

triage.headline_ja: サンカルロス市、デング熱症例が98%減少
triage.triage_reason: デング熱症例数が前年比98%減少という好調な傾向を報告する内容であり、公衆衛生上の異常な脅威や国際的拡大リスクは認められない。
triage.notes: 記事は症例減少という好転傾向の報告であり、シグナルとしての緊急性は低い。チクングニア・ジカ・黄熱の症例は「discarded（否定）」と報告されている。

article.articleHeadline: UK Aid Worker Evacuated After Possible Ebola Exposure in DR Congo
article.articleSummary: UK humanitarian worker evacuated to London after possible occupational exposure to Ebola (Bundibugyo virus) during outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The worker, a UK resident, is asymptomatic and in strict isolation during the 2–21 day incubation period; transported on a dedicated medical evacuation flight for specialist assessment. UK Health Security Agency says no confirmed cases in the UK and public risk remains low. The current outbreak in DRC and Uganda is the 17th Ebola outbreak in DRC and the third-largest on record, with 2,473 confirmed cases and 999 deaths in DRC, plus 20 cases and 2 deaths in Uganda (as of 20 July 2026), totaling 2,494 cases and 1,001 deaths. Transmission is via direct contact with blood or body fluids, not airborne. Ongoing outbreak factors include conflict, limited healthcare, and cross-border movement; authorities emphasize surveillance and precautionary measures.

triage.headline_ja: 英国の援助従事者、コンゴ民主共和国でのエボラ曝露疑いによりロンドンへ搬送
triage.triage_reason: DRC・ウガンダでの大規模エボラ流行（計2,494例、1,001死亡、過去3番目の規模）に加え、英国人援助者の国際搬送事案が発生しており、IHR基準の複数該当と国際的関心の高さからフルRRAへ進めるべき。
triage.notes: 記事の主題はDRC（および一部ウガンダ）における進行中のエボラ（ブンディブギョ株）アウトブレイク。英国・ロンドン・イングランドは搬送先であり発生国ではないため verified_locations から除外。ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola : la RDC dépasse le seuil de 1000 décès
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola: the DRC surpasses the 1,000-death threshold.
article.articleSummary: Democratic Republic of the Congo reports 2,536 confirmed Ebola cases and 1,033 deaths, a 40.7% case fatality rate, as of July 21, 2026, per the Ministry of Health outbreak bulletin. About 738 patients are currently isolated or hospitalized, and 506 have recovered. Contact tracing stands at 77.2% completed. The five affected provinces are Haut-Uele, Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, and Tshopo, with Ituri as the principal hotspot. Authorities have strengthened field teams, laboratory capacity, and health facilities there, and have intensified contact-tracing, entry-point surveillance, and community outreach, supported by logistics and medical resources to consolidate the on-the-ground response and curb transmission as the outbreak persists across these provinces.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱:コンゴ民主共和国、死者数1000人の閾値を超える
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱の大規模流行(2536症例、致死率40.7%)が5州に拡大しており、IHR基準・WPRO基準の複数に該当する重大な公衆衛生事象である。
triage.notes: コンゴ民主共和国北キブ州は対象国リストの座標情報にあるが、対象国自体(203312)がリストに含まれているため国単位で計上。死者1000人超・致死率40.7%と非常に深刻であり、国際的な支援・監視が必要な状況。

article.articleHeadline: Kongo'da Ebola alarmı büyüyor! Can kaybı 1000'i geçti - Radikal
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola alarm grows in Congo! Death toll surpasses 1,000.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (Ituri, eastern region) reports 2,536 laboratory-confirmed cases and 1,033 deaths; 738 patients are in isolation or receiving hospital treatment. The current epidemic is linked to the Bundibugyo Ebola virus variant, with a case fatality rate updated to 40.7%. The outbreak began May 15 after 246 suspected cases and 65 deaths were reported in Ituri, prompting an official declaration. The WHO declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern on May 17. There is no approved treatment or vaccine. Ebola is a viral hemorrhagic fever. Historical context notes the virus’ first identified outbreaks in 1976 near Nzara and Yambuku, and the 2013–2017 West Africa epidemic (Guinea, Liberia, Sierra Leone) with about 30,000 cases and over 11,000 deaths. The ongoing eastern Congo outbreak raises ongoing public health concerns due to the virulent Bundibugyo variant.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴでエボラ警報拡大！死者数1000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国（イトゥリ州）で確定症例2,536件・死者1,033人、致死率40.7%のエボラ（ブンディブジョ株）流行が継続しWHOがPHEICを宣言しており、複数のIHR基準に該当する重大シグナルである。
triage.notes: 記事中のスーダン、シエラレオネ、リベリア、ギニア、ブルンジ、ヤンブク等は1976年初発地や2013-2017年西アフリカ流行の歴史的言及であり、現行の流行地域ではないためverified_locationsから除外した。承認済み治療薬・ワクチンが存在しない点も重大なリスク要因。

article.articleHeadline: Why health officials do not have a good handle on the current Ebola outbreak
article.articleSummary: As of July 23, 2026, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo continues with no approved vaccine. In just over two months, more than 1,000 people have died and over 2,400 have been sickened; daily cases show no slowdown. More than 80% of new cases occur outside known contacts, indicating undetected transmission. Contact tracing—mapping every contact of a sick person—remains labor-intensive and challenging in a region of conflict with transient workers. WHO is training about 21,000 community workers to bolster surveillance. About two-thirds of deaths occur outside health facilities, with many patients seeking traditional healers or delaying care due to mistrust and stigma. Trials for treatments and a post-exposure drug offer hope, but access remains limited to clinical studies.

triage.headline_ja: 現行のエボラ出血熱アウトブレイクを保健当局が十分に掌握できていない理由
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で2か月余りに1,000人超が死亡、2,400人超が感染し、新規症例の80%以上が既知の接触者外で発生するなど拡大が制御できていない重大な流行であり、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するためフルRRAへ進むべき。
triage.notes: 承認済みワクチンがなく、接触者追跡が紛争地域と流動的な労働者のため困難。死亡の約3分の2が医療施設外で発生し、伝統療法者への依存や不信・スティグマが遅延受診の一因。WHOは約21,000人の地域保健従事者を訓練中。

article.articleHeadline: Ölümcül salgında can kaybı 1000'i geçti! Aşısı ve tedavisi yok
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Death toll in a deadly outbreak has surpassed 1,000! There is no vaccine or treatment.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (Ituri Province, eastern DRC) has 2,536 confirmed cases and 1,033 deaths, with 738 patients in isolation or hospital care. The outbreak is caused by the rare Bundibugyo Ebola virus variant, with a case fatality rate around 40.7%. Ituri reports 246 suspected cases and 65 deaths, and the outbreak was declared on May 15. The World Health Organization declared a public health emergency of international concern on May 17. There is no approved therapy or vaccine for Bundibugyo Ebola virus infection. Ebola is a viral hemorrhagic fever; it was first identified in 1976 in Nzara (South Sudan) and Yambuku (near the Ebola River). The 2014–2017 West Africa outbreak in Guinea, Liberia, and Sierra Leone infected about 30,000 people and killed over 11,000. Ongoing vigilance is required.

triage.headline_ja: 致死性の流行で死者数が1000人を超えた！ワクチンも治療法もない
triage.triage_reason: DRCイツリ州でエボラ(ブンディブギョ株)の大規模流行が発生し、死者1,000人超・致死率約40%、WHOがPHEICを宣言しており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する。
triage.notes: 発生地域リストにはSudan, Sierra Leone, Liberia, Burundi等が含まれるが、これらは疾患の歴史的背景（1976年発見地、2014-2017年西アフリカ流行）として言及されているのみで、今回の流行地はDRCイツリ州に限定される。WHOはPHEICを宣言済み(2026-05-17)。

article.articleHeadline: Спалах Еболи: у Конго фіксують найстрімкіше зростання смертей, люди опираються стримуванню хвороби
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak: Congo records the fastest rise in deaths, people resist efforts to contain the disease.
article.articleSummary: An Ebola virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has caused 1,031 deaths among 2,473 diagnosed cases, with 737 suspected, since the 17th outbreak began in May 2026. The Bundibugyo virus is implicated, and there are no vaccines or therapies for this strain. The rapid mortality exceeds patterns from 2013–2016, with WHO estimates that true case numbers could be two to four times higher than reported. About 80% of new infections occur outside known transmission chains, and resistance to safe burials elevates transmission risk. Armed conflict and hostile settings hinder response; humanitarian workers face attacks, and some areas lack timely care. Lab results can take more than four days, delaying diagnosis. In the first month after outbreak declaration, 267 people died and over 1,000 were infected. Trials of potential treatments are underway.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ流行:コンゴで死者数の急増が最速に、住民は封じ込め対策に抵抗
triage.triage_reason: DRCでエボラ(ブンディブギョ株)の致死率の高いアウトブレイクが拡大しており、ワクチン・治療法が存在せず、武装紛争や埋葬拒否により制御が困難で国際的拡大リスクも懸念されるため。
triage.notes: ワクチン・治療法がないブンディブギョ株による高致死率のアウトブレイクで、武装紛争地域での対応困難、80%が既知の感染経路外での感染という点から、フルリスク評価が必要と判断。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola-Epidemie im Kongo überschreitet Marke von 1000 Toten
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola epidemic in the Congo surpasses 1,000 deaths.
article.articleSummary: By July 23, 2026, the Democratic Republic of Congo’s latest Ebola outbreak—the 17th in the country—has reached 1,033 deaths and 2,536 confirmed infections, with 63 new cases and 34 deaths since the prior report. It is driven by the Bundibugyo variant, with case fatality up to 40%; there is no licensed vaccine or therapy for Bundibugyo. Transmission is via direct contact with bodily fluids, causing fever, vomiting and, in severe cases, bleeding. Several experimental vaccines/therapies are in evaluation; Oxford University began a safety trial of the ChAdOx1 vaccine. The security situation in eastern DRC severely hampers response: attacks on health facilities and staff, with 80% of new cases outside known transmission chains and more than 60% of deaths occurring before medical care. Uganda reports 20 cases; borders were closed for about four weeks, and the last patient in Uganda was discharged on July 16, triggering a 42-day countdown to virus-free status.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ流行、死者1,000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: DRCで大規模なエボラ流行(死者1,033人、感染2,536人)が継続し、ワクチン未承認の変異株、国境を越えたウガンダへの拡大、治安悪化による対応困難など複数のIHR基準に該当するため。
triage.notes: ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsから除外。ただし国際的拡大の事実（越境事例、国境閉鎖）はIHR基準の判断に反映した。

article.articleHeadline: В результате вспышки лихорадки Эбола в Демократической Республике Конго скончались более тысячи человек
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: More than 1,000 people have died in an Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo continues with 2,473 cases and at least 1,031 deaths reported by the DRC Ministry of Health as of July 23, 2026; about 737 patients are in isolation or receiving treatment. The World Health Organization classifies this as the third-largest Ebola outbreak in DRC history. The epicenter is Ituri Province in eastern DRC, with the outbreak beginning on May 15 and cross-border spread to Uganda noted. Public health responders cite lack of vaccines, medicines, and funding as contributors to high fatalities, according to Africa CDC Director-General Jean Kasaiya. In response, Oxford University launched the world’s first clinical trials of a vaccine targeting Bundibugyo ebolavirus—the strain driving this outbreak—last week, marking an urgent step toward containment.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国でのエボラ出血熱流行により1000人以上が死亡
triage.triage_reason: DRC史上3番目に大きいエボラ流行で死者1000人超、ウガンダへの越境拡大も確認されており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する重大シグナル。
triage.notes: ウガンダへの越境拡大が記載されているが、ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsには含めていない。ワクチン・医薬品・資金不足が致死率上昇の要因とされ、Oxford大学によるBundibugyoエボラウイルス株を標的とした臨床試験が開始されている。

article.articleHeadline: Hanseníase ainda registra muitos casos no Acre e diagnóstico precoce é essencial
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Hansen's disease still records many cases in Acre, and early diagnosis is essential.
article.articleSummary: Hansen's disease (leprosy) remains a reality in Acre, Brazil, with emphasis on early diagnosis. Dermatologist Dr. Camila Costa, on the Médico24Horas program, highlighted the importance of prompt detection. The Fundação Hospitalar has a dedicated unit for patients with suspected cases, where individuals undergo testing and, if confirmed, begin free treatment through the Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS). The report notes ongoing cases in Acre and the availability of free, government-funded care upon confirmation. No specific case counts are provided. The arrangement illustrates a public health response ensuring access to diagnostic testing and treatment for Hansen's disease in the state. As of July 23, 2026, this framework supports prompt testing and treatment.

triage.headline_ja: アクレ州でハンセン病の症例が依然として多く報告され、早期診断が重要
triage.triage_reason: ハンセン病はブラジル・アクレ州の地域医療における既知の風土病であり、通常の啓発報道であって異常性・国際的拡大リスクは認められない。
triage.notes: 具体的な症例数の記載はなく、既存の公衆衛生対応（SUSによる無料診断・治療）に関する一般的な啓発記事。

article.articleHeadline: Эпидемиолог Никифоров пояснил, что вирус Эбола передается только при тесном контакте
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Epidemiologist Nikiforov explained that the Ebola virus is transmitted only through close contact.
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-07-23, Ebola remains endemic to the Congo and neighboring countries and does not pose a global threat, according to Vladimir Nikiforov, head of infectious diseases and epidemiology at Pyrogov NMRC. The virus is linked to fruit bats that inhabit environments around 30°C and feed on bananas and mangoes. Nikiforov stresses that Ebola is not transmitted via airborne routes; infection occurs only through very close contact. The disease has been known since the 1980s and has not spread widely beyond the Congo. The statements were reported by Zvezdanews; no current outbreaks, case counts, or laboratory confirmations are described in the article.

triage.headline_ja: 疫学者ニキフォロフ氏、エボラウイルスは濃厚接触でのみ感染すると説明
triage.triage_reason: 現在の具体的な発生や症例数の報告はなく、専門家がエボラの伝播様式について一般的な解説を行っている記事であり、シグナルとしての緊急性は認められない。
triage.notes: 記事は専門家によるエボラの伝播様式に関する一般的な解説であり、コンゴでの現在進行中の発生を報告するものではない。具体的な症例数や新規発生の記述がないため、DRCも含め対象国は該当なしとした。

article.articleHeadline: 2026年湖南省蚊媒传染病防控区域中心（永州）疫情防控应急演练暨培训班在永州举行_健康_永州站
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: 2026 Hunan Province Mosquito-borne Infectious Disease Prevention and Control Regional Center (Yongzhou) Emergency Drill and Training Course on Epidemic Prevention and Control Held in Yongzhou
article.articleSummary: On July 21–23, 2026, Yongzhou, Hunan Province hosted the 2026 Hunan Province Mosquito-borne Infectious Disease Prevention and Control Regional Center (Yongzhou) Epidemic Prevention and Control Emergency Drill and Training. Organized by the Yongzhou Health Commission and conducted by the Yongzhou Center for Disease Control and Prevention, with participation from Hengyang and Chenzhou authorities, the exercise aims to strengthen regional coordination against dengue and chikungunya. It promotes a unified framework for rapid response, precise prevention, and closed-loop management across the three southern Hunan cities. Training covered Aedes mosquito biology, vector surveillance and control, the 'Two Heat' prevention strategies, and fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome management. Drills combined tabletop simulations (outbreak reporting, on-site response, risk zoning, media communication) with field activities (household surveys, vector monitoring, disinfection). Next steps will sustain the regional center and expand cross-city preventive measures to fortify public health security.

triage.headline_ja: 2026年湖南省蚊媒感染症予防制御地域センター（永州）疫病予防制御緊急訓練及び研修が永州で開催
triage.triage_reason: 実際の疫病発生ではなく、蚊媒介感染症対策の訓練・研修に関する行政広報記事であるため。
triage.notes: 記事は実際の感染症発生事例ではなく、予防訓練・研修活動の報告記事。デング熱・チクングニア熱の実際の症例発生は言及されていない。

article.articleHeadline: Cúm mùa có thể nguy hiểm hơn bạn nghĩ , bác sĩ cấp cứu cảnh báo điều gì?
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Seasonal flu may be more dangerous than you think — what are emergency doctors warning about?
article.articleSummary: Seasonal influenza can be more dangerous than commonly thought, warn emergency physicians in Vietnam. While usually mild, influenza can cause pneumonia, respiratory failure, myocarditis, and death, even among young and healthy individuals. Dr. Nguyen Trung Cap, Associate Professor and Deputy Director of the National Institute of Tropical Diseases, outlines warning signs for urgent admission, common self-treatment mistakes, and the role of vaccination in preventing complications. At the Emergency Department, severe flu cases are frequently admitted; influenza in high-risk groups (elderly and those with cardiovascular, pulmonary, or metabolic diseases like diabetes) can trigger a systemic crisis. Influenza increases myocardial infarction risk 6–10× and stroke 8×; diabetics with flu are hospitalized up to 6×, with mortality 2–3× higher. Elderly may lose autonomy; severe cases may require ICU, ventilation, dialysis, or ECMO, with costs of tens to hundreds of millions VND. Common errors: viewing flu as trivial and self-medicating with antibiotics or corticosteroids; vaccination and preventive measures are emphasized.

triage.headline_ja: 季節性インフルエンザは思っているより危険かもしれない――救急医が警告する内容とは
triage.triage_reason: 特定のアウトブレイクや異常な感染急増を報告するものではなく、季節性インフルエンザの重症化リスクに関する一般的な医療啓発記事であるため。
triage.notes: 記事は季節性インフルエンザの合併症リスクについての医師による一般的な注意喚起であり、具体的な発生数・地域的流行状況の記載はない。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola outbreak with no vaccine or treatment spreading too fast to contain, doctors warn
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, caused by Bundibugyo virus, is spreading too fast to contain. As of 22 July, more than 1,000 people have died. Cases have been confirmed in five provinces, with the outbreak largely centered in remote Ituri province. There are no vaccines or specific treatments for Bundibugyo virus. Officials warn that roughly 80% of new cases arise outside known transmission chains, indicating rapid spread beyond tracing capacity. The outbreak is described as the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in history, outpacing the 2013–2016 West Africa epidemic, which killed over 11,000 people. Published 2026-07-23. Ongoing and unchecked.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱の流行、ワクチンも治療法もなく拡大を制御できないと医師らが警告
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国でのブンディブギョウイルスによるエボラ流行が1000人以上の死者を出し、複数州に拡大、追跡不能な感染が8割を占めるなど深刻かつ異常な事態であり、IHR基準を複数満たす。
triage.notes: アンゴラは発生地域に含まれるが記事本文では言及がなく、対象国リストにも含まれないため除外。史上最速の拡大速度とされ、ワクチン・治療法が存在しない点が特に懸念材料。

article.articleHeadline: Doença fatal em bovinos acende alerta no Oeste de SC e mobiliza Cidasc
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Fatal disease in cattle triggers alert in western Santa Catarina and mobilizes CIDASC.
article.articleSummary: Rabies confirmed in cattle in Itapiranga, far western Santa Catarina, Brazil, renewing state-wide vigilance as CIDASC reports a new suspected case in the same region. Santa Catarina is endemic for rabies; the virus circulates mainly via hematophagous bats (Desmodus rotundus), so vaccination remains essential. CIDASC urges immediate vaccination of animals on the affected property and neighboring properties to curb spread, given bat vectors can move between properties in days. The disease also poses a human health risk; avoid contact with neurologically affected animals and contact CIDASC for veterinary evaluation and laboratory testing. Clinical signs in cattle include ataxia, excessive salivation, apathy, isolation from the herd, anorexia, and progressive paralysis culminating in death; confirmation requires laboratory analysis of brain tissue post-mortem. In 2026, 26 rabies cases in production animals have been recorded across multiple municipalities, with activity concentrated in the southern and western regions, including Itapiranga, Chapecó, and São José do Cedro.

triage.headline_ja: サンタカタリーナ州西部で牛の致死性疾患が警戒を呼び起こし、CIDASCが動員
triage.triage_reason: 牛における狂犬病流行地域内での複数症例確認であり、人間への感染は現時点で報告されていないが、コウモリを媒介とした継続的な曝露リスクがあるため経過観察が必要。
triage.notes: 本事案は主に家畜（牛）における狂犬病流行であり、ブラジル・サンタカタリーナ州は狂犬病の風土病地域。吸血コウモリ（Desmodus rotundus）が主な媒介動物。人間への感染例は報告されていないが、神経症状を示す動物との接触回避が呼びかけられており、人畜共通感染症としての監視が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola outbreak with no vaccine spreading too fast to contain, doctors warn
article.articleSummary: DRC Ebola outbreak driven by Bundibugyo virus is spreading too fast to contain, doctors warn. As of 22 July, more than 1,000 people have died in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. There are no vaccines or specific treatments for Bundibugyo virus. Cases have been confirmed in five provinces, with the outbreak most concentrated in remote Ituri province. Officials say 80% of new cases have emerged outside known transmission chains, indicating the outbreak is expanding faster than contact tracing can track. The current outbreak has killed more people at a faster rate than any previous Ebola outbreak, including the 2013–2016 West Africa outbreak, which caused more than 11,000 deaths. This underscores the urgent need for intensified clinical and public health responses across affected areas.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱の発生、ワクチンなく感染拡大が制御不能なほど速いと医師らが警告
triage.triage_reason: ワクチン・治療法がないBundibugyoウイルスによるエボラ流行がDRC5州に拡大し、1,000人以上が死亡、伝播経路不明の症例が80%に達するなど公衆衛生上深刻かつ異常事態であり、国際的拡大リスクも高い。
triage.notes: ワクチン・特異的治療法が存在しないBundibugyo型エボラウイルスによる過去最大規模・最速の致死率を示す流行。5州に拡大し、80%が既知の感染経路外という異常な拡大速度を示している。

article.articleHeadline: Woman loses part of toe after rat bite at TN govt hospital
article.articleSummary: In Tiruchirappalli, Tamil Nadu, a 70-year-old woman, R Tamilkodi of Alathur near Kalkandarkottai, lost part of her left big toe after a rat bit it in the post-operative ward of Mahatma Gandhi Memorial Government Hospital. She had surgery for a left ankle injury sustained in a July 20 fall; the toe bite occurred on July 23. Hospital officials said staff cleaned the wound, administered tetanus and other preventive vaccines, and the patient’s vitals were stable. Her son, Vijayakumar, reported rats in the ward and criticized the lack of action prior to the incident. Rodent-control measures have since been initiated. AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami condemned the government’s hospital maintenance and referenced the chief minister C. Joseph Vijay’s film Jana Nayagan. The report emphasizes infection risks in hospital settings, with no confirmation of other infections beyond the tetanus prophylaxis.

triage.headline_ja: タミル・ナードゥ州の政府病院でネズミに噛まれ、女性がつま先の一部を失う
triage.triage_reason: 個別患者に対する病院内でのネズミ咬傷事故であり、感染症の公衆衛生上のアウトブレイクではないため、トリアージ基準に該当しない。
triage.notes: 破傷風は予防接種として投与されたのみで、実際の破傷風感染例ではない。病院の衛生管理問題として政治的批判の対象となっているが、感染症サーベイランスの対象事象ではない。

article.articleHeadline: कांगो में तेजी से बढ़ रहा इबोला का प्रकोप!: स्वास्थ्य अधिकारी भी फेल? 1,000 से ज्यादा लोगों की गई जान | Ebola outbreak surging in Congo! Have health officials failed too? Over 1,000 lives lost.
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak surging in Congo! Have health officials failed too? Over 1,000 lives lost.
article.articleSummary: Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo is spreading rapidly, with over 1,000 deaths confirmed. At a health conference in Ghana, Africa CDC Director Dr. Jean Kaseya stated the outbreak has claimed 1,031 lives. The DRC’s health ministry reports 2,473 cases to date, with at least 737 patients in isolation or hospital. The World Health Organization says the true scale could be two to four times higher than official counts, noting the outbreak began on May 15 and has accelerated since. Officials warn that 80% of new cases occur outside known transmission chains, indicating untracked spread and containment challenges. Authorities point to a lack of vaccines, medicines, and funding as key factors driving mortality. The updates reflect ongoing, uncontained Ebola transmission within the Democratic Republic of Congo.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴでエボラ感染急増！保健当局も対応失敗か？死者1,000人超え
triage.triage_reason: DRCで確認死者1,000人超・症例2,473件に達し、新規感染の8割が既知の感染連鎖外で発生するなど封じ込め困難な状況であり、IHR基準・WPRO基準の複数に該当する。
triage.notes: ガーナはAfrica CDCディレクターが会見を行った開催地であり、実際のアウトブレイク発生国ではないためverified_locationsから除外した。WHOは実際の規模が公式発表の2〜4倍に達する可能性を指摘しており、ワクチン・医薬品・資金不足が死亡率上昇の要因とされる。続報を要フォロー。
